nodes.title: Deyga or Vilvah: which natural brand suits your skin?
nodes.body:
If you are looking for natural skincare in the UK with roots in Indian beauty traditions, two names come up again and again: Deyga and Vilvah. Both are Indian brands, both work with plant-based and kitchen-cupboard ingredients, and Swansura is an official UK partner of both, so every product is genuine and ships from the UK. They are not the same, though. Here is how to tell which one suits your skin, and where to start. For the ingredients behind both, read our Indian skincare guide.

The short answer

Choose Vilvah if you like creamy, comforting textures built around goat milk, oat milk and gentle botanicals. Choose Deyga if you prefer farm-grown herbs, clays, charcoal and fruit actives with a fresher feel. Many people end up using both: a Vilvah cleanser or serum in the morning and a Deyga treat, such as a lip balm or face pack, alongside it.

Vilvah: goat milk and botanical care

Vilvah is known for milk-based formulas for face, hair and body. The best place to start is Vilvah Milk Drops Hydrating Serum, a lightweight milk serum with natural milk proteins that sinks in quickly and leaves skin feeling soft rather than greasy. It is the product people search for most: "Vilvah Milk Drops" is one of the brand's top searches in the UK. Our Vilvah Milk Drops guide goes through its ingredients and the 20ml and 40ml sizes.

For hair, the Vilvah Goat Milk Shampoo pairs goat milk with pea protein and jasmine. It is pH-balanced and free from artificial colours and fragrances, so it suits frequent washing, and it is a good fit for dry or frizzy hair. If you want the full ritual, the Goat Milk Hair Kit puts the shampoo with its partners in one box. Our natural shampoo guide compares more options.

For the body, Vilvah Milk Body Lotion uses oat milk, ceramides and olive squalane in a quick-absorbing, vegan formula that is gentle enough for the whole family. Prefer a no-scent wash? The Fragrance-Free Cream Face Wash is the calmest place to begin. See the whole range on our goat milk edit.

Deyga: farm-grown botanicals

Deyga makes natural skin, hair and body care with plant-based ingredients, many grown on its own farm in India. Its cult favourite is the Deyga Beetroot Lip Balm: beetroot extract and natural butters give a soft, sheer tint, and the 10 g tin fits any pocket. "Deyga lip balm" is one of the brand's most searched products, and it makes an easy first try at under £11. Not sure whether to buy the pot or the stick? Read Deyga Beetroot Lip Balm: stick or pot.

For oilier or combination skin, the Deyga Charcoal Face Wash uses activated charcoal for a deep, refreshing cleanse without a tight finish. For glow, the Deyga Rose Glow Serum is a light rose and saffron oil serum that leaves skin looking radiant. On wash day, Deyga Rice Water Shampoo is a gentle, sulfate-free everyday cleanser.

Which is better for your skin type?

Dry or sensitive skin

Lean towards Vilvah. Milk textures, fragrance-free options and the oat milk body lotion are made for comfort. Add a Deyga body butter for dry skin, such as the Chocolate Body Butter, for extra richness on elbows and legs.

Oily or combination skin

Start with Deyga's charcoal face wash and a lightweight serum, then use a Vilvah milk product only where skin feels dry. Our face wash for oily skin page compares the options side by side, and our guide to face wash for your skin type explains how to choose.

Dull-looking skin

Try one serum from each brand on alternate days: Vilvah Milk Drops for hydration and Deyga Rose Glow for radiance. Keep everything else simple.

A simple routine using both brands

  1. Cleanse: Deyga Charcoal Face Wash (oilier skin) or Vilvah Fragrance-Free Cream Face Wash (drier skin).
  2. Treat: Vilvah Milk Drops in the morning, Deyga Rose Glow in the evening.
  3. Lips and body: Deyga Beetroot Lip Balm through the day and Vilvah Milk Body Lotion after showering.

Patch test anything new and introduce one product at a time. Ready-made pairings with 5% off are on our routines page.

Why buy Deyga and Vilvah from Swansura?

We are an official UK partner of both brands, so there are no grey imports and no long waits from abroad: orders are dispatched from the UK, usually within 1–2 working days, with free UK delivery over £40. Explore the full natural skincare edit, or go straight to all Deyga and all Vilvah products. New to either brand? Start with our Deyga Organics guide or our Vilvah guide.

nodes.title: How to layer oud with body butter so it lasts all day
nodes.body:
Oud is one of the richest notes in perfumery: smoky, resinous and warm. Yet even a great oud perfume can fade sooner than you expect on dry skin. The fix is simple and costs very little: layer it over a body butter. Here is why it works, how to do it, and three pairings from our shelves to try.

Why fragrance lasts longer on moisturised skin

Perfume oils evaporate fastest from dry skin. A thin layer of butter or lotion gives the fragrance something to cling to, so it tends to unfold more slowly and stay closer to you for longer. Rich butters with cocoa, shea or almond oil work especially well under warm notes such as oud, amber and vanilla. If your skin runs dry, a body butter for dry skin does two jobs at once.

How to layer, step by step

  1. Shower first. Pat skin almost dry; slightly damp skin takes butter more evenly.
  2. Warm a little butter between your palms and press it into pulse points: wrists, inner elbows, the base of the neck and behind the knees.
  3. Wait a minute so the butter settles.
  4. Spray once or twice from about 15 cm onto the same spots. Don't rub your wrists together; let it dry.
  5. Top up the butter, not the perfume, later in the day if skin feels dry. The scent often comes back with it.

Three skin + scent pairings to try

1. Sweet and golden: Chocolate Body Butter + Amber Oud Gold

The Deyga Chocolate Body Butter is made with cocoa and nourishing oils and has a light chocolate scent. Under Al Haramain Amber Oud Gold Edition, with its melon, pineapple, vanilla and musk, it reads as a soft gourmand. For more intensity, try the Amber Oud Extreme Gold Edition extrait. "Chocolate body butter" and "Al Haramain Amber Oud" are both popular UK searches, and this is the pairing that shows why.

2. Floral and warm: Rose & Geranium Body Butter + Amber Oud Ruby

The Deyga Rose & Geranium Body Butter carries rose and geranium essential oils. Layer it under Al Haramain Amber Oud Ruby Edition, which opens with saffron and bitter almond over jasmine, cedarwood, ambergris and musk, and the florals meet in the middle. If you love rose with oud, Montale Aoud Damascus is another lovely match.

3. Clean and smoky: a light lotion + Gucci Intense Oud

Not every pairing needs a scented base. A light, quick-absorbing lotion such as Vilvah Milk Body Lotion lets a dark scent like Gucci Intense Oud (black pepper, incense, woods, leather and an oud accord) lead the way, while still giving it something to hold on to. Want a luxury option? Try Highborn London Natural Luminosity Body Butter.

Which base suits your skin?

If your skin is very dry, a rich butter such as Deyga's cocoa or rose formulas gives the most staying power. If you prefer something lighter in warm weather, a lotion like Deyga Almond Milk Body Lotion absorbs faster and still helps the fragrance last. On sensitive days, keep the base unscented and let the perfume do the talking.

A few tips for oud

  • Less is more. Oud projects well; one or two sprays over butter usually lasts.
  • Spray clothes lightly, not silk, to keep a soft trail.
  • Match the mood. Sweet butters suit amber ouds, floral butters suit rose ouds, and neutral lotions suit smoky ouds.

New to oud and Arabian perfume? Our guide to Lattafa Khamrah Qahwa and Arabian perfume explains the notes and how to choose. To pick an Amber Oud edition, see every Al Haramain Amber Oud edition compared. For Tom Ford Oud Wood, Gucci Intense Oud and other designer ouds, see our oud perfume guide.

Browse every oud perfume we stock, the full oud scent family, or our body butter edit. Each pairing above also makes a thoughtful gift, and orders over £40 ship free across the UK.

nodes.title: Extrait vs eau de parfum: what the label means
nodes.body:
Extrait de parfum, eau de parfum, eau de toilette: the words on the bottle tell you how concentrated the fragrance is. That affects how long it lasts, how far it travels and, often, the price. Here is what each label means and how to choose.

The labels, from strongest to lightest

Extrait de parfum (also "parfum")

The most concentrated form, typically around 20–40% perfume oil. Extraits sit close to the skin, develop slowly and can last from morning to evening. Italian house Tiziana Terenzi is known for them: Kaff Extrait de Parfum opens with bergamot, juniper and white iris before lavender, magnolia and leather settle into amber, musk and woods. Tiziana Terenzi Kirke, one of the house's most searched perfumes in the UK, is a fruity extrait, and Gold Rose Oudh brings rose and oud together.

Eau de parfum (EDP)

Usually around 15–20% perfume oil, and the most popular strength today. An EDP has good projection and wears for several hours. Good examples: Al Haramain Amber Oud Gold Edition and Calvin Klein Eternity Eau de Parfum.

Eau de toilette (EDT)

Lighter, typically around 5–15%, with a bright opening that suits daytime and warm weather. Try Calvin Klein Eternity for Men Eau de Toilette or Davidoff Champion.

These ranges are typical, not fixed rules. Every house sets its own formula, which is why one brand's EDP can outlast another's extrait.

Same name, different strength

Many perfumes come in more than one concentration, and they don't always smell identical. Al Haramain's Amber Oud Gold Edition eau de parfum and the Amber Oud Extreme Gold Edition extrait share the same fruity amber notes, but the extrait feels richer and closer to the skin. Calvin Klein's Eternity comes as an EDT, an EDP and a parfum miniature, which is an easy way to compare. Two popular examples, side by side: Dior Sauvage EDT vs EDP vs Parfum and Calvin Klein Eternity for women vs for men. Versace Eros eau de toilette and Eros Parfum are compared in our Versace perfume guide.

Which should you choose?

  • For all-day wear and evenings: an extrait, or an EDP layered over body butter.
  • For the office and everyday: an EDP, with one or two sprays.
  • For hot weather or the gym bag: an EDT, which you can reapply freely.
  • For gifting: an EDP is the safe choice; a travel-size mini lets someone try a new strength first.

Other words you might see on the label

  • Intense, Extreme or Elixir: a richer version of an existing scent. It is often closer to an extrait in feel, but there is no fixed rule, so check the notes.
  • Cologne or eau de cologne: the lightest style, usually fresh and citrusy, made for a quick lift.
  • ml: the bottle size. A 10 ml miniature is a low-cost way to test a scent on your own skin before buying 100 ml.

How to make any concentration last longer

Whatever the label says, skin matters. Fragrance tends to last longer on moisturised skin, so apply a little body lotion or butter to pulse points first, then spray. Keep bottles out of sunlight and heat, and avoid rubbing your wrists together. Our guide to layering oud with body butter walks through it step by step, and the body lotion for dry skin edit has easy bases to try.

Is extrait worth the price?

Per spray, often yes: you use less, and it lasts longer. But "stronger" doesn't mean "better". Choose the scent first and the concentration second. nodes.title: Aloe vera gel: how to use it on your face, hair and body
nodes.body:
Aloe vera gel is one of the most searched skincare products in the UK, and it is easy to see why. One jar can work as a light moisturiser, a cooling layer after a day outdoors, a leave-in for hair and an after-shower gel for the body. Here is what to look for when you buy it, and how to use it on your face, hair and body.

What is aloe vera gel?

Aloe vera gel comes from the clear, jelly-like inside of the leaves of the aloe plant (Aloe barbadensis on an ingredient list). It is mostly water, which is why it feels so light: it sinks in quickly and does not leave a greasy film. A good gel is clear or very pale, with a soft, wobbly texture that melts when you spread it.

What to look for in a jar

  • Aloe first on the list. The first ingredient should be aloe vera juice or aloe leaf extract, not water.
  • A short ingredient list. Aloe gels need little else: a thickener to make the gel and a preservative to keep it safe once opened.
  • No added fragrance or colour if your skin is sensitive. A green tint usually means a dye has been added.

Vilvah Aloe Vera Gel (100ml, from £9.99) ticks all three. Its full ingredient list is just four items: aloe vera juice, xanthan gum, guar gum and Geogard ECT, a natural preservative. It is free from harsh alcohols, silicones and synthetic fragrance, and it is made by Vilvah, one of our official partner brands, and dispatched from the UK.

How to use aloe vera gel on your face

  • As a light moisturiser. After cleansing, smooth a pea-sized amount over damp skin. On oily or combination skin this may be all you need; on dry skin, follow with your usual cream.
  • Under your serum or cream. A thin layer first gives your routine extra slip, and serums such as Vilvah Milk Drops (from £21.99) spread easily over it.
  • As a quick mask. Apply a thicker layer for 10 minutes, then rinse or press the rest into the skin. For clay, charcoal and powder masks, see our face mask guide.
  • After a day outdoors. A cool layer feels comforting on skin that has had a lot of sun or wind. Keep the jar in the fridge for an extra-cool feel.

In the morning, aloe gel is not a sunscreen, so finish with SPF, such as Vilvah Skin Finish Sunscreen SPF 50 PA+++ (£17.99).

A simple routine with aloe vera gel

  1. Cleanse with a gentle face wash such as Vilvah Fragrance-Free Cream Face Wash (£9.99) or the Vilvah Honey Face Wash (£12.99). Not sure which? See face wash for your skin type.
  2. Tone with a mist of Deyga Pure Rose Water Toner (£11.99).
  3. Hydrate with aloe vera gel.
  4. Protect with sunscreen in the morning, or a richer cream at night if your skin is dry.

Prefer it ready-made? The Vilvah Sensitive Skin Kit (£29.99) pairs a steam-distilled rose toner with the aloe gel, and the Vilvah Anti-Acne Kit (£25.99) pairs the Honey Face Wash with the aloe gel for oily skin. You will find more routines on our routines page.

How to use aloe vera gel on your hair

  • As a light leave-in. Smooth a small amount through damp lengths and ends to tame flyaways and add shine without weighing hair down.
  • As a soft styling gel. Use it to smooth a ponytail or define curls, without the crunch of a styling gel.
  • With a serum. For very frizzy hair, mix a little gel with a drop of Vilvah Anti-Frizz Hair Serum (£28.99) and comb through with a wide-tooth neem wood comb (£13.99).

For more ideas, see our hair serums for frizzy hair and haircare.

How to use aloe vera gel on your body

  • After a shower, as a light, fast-drying layer on warm days.
  • After shaving or hair removal, for a cool, fresh feel on the skin.
  • Under body lotion on dry skin: let the gel sink in, then lock it in with a cream such as Vilvah Milk Body Lotion (£25.99), made with oat milk, ceramides and olive squalane.

Good to know

  • Patch test first. Apply a little to your inner arm and wait 24 hours, especially if your skin is sensitive.
  • Use clean hands or a spatula and close the jar after use, so the gel stays fresh. Check the pack for how long it lasts once opened.
  • Sunburn or a skin condition? Speak to a pharmacist or your GP. Aloe gel is a cosmetic, not a treatment.

nodes.title: Body scrub: how to choose one and how often to use it
nodes.body:
A body scrub is the quickest way to make skin feel smoother. It buffs away the dry, dull surface layer, so skin feels softer straight away and your body lotion or butter spreads more easily afterwards. But scrubs are not all the same: some are creamy, some are gritty, some are powders you mix yourself. Here is how to choose a body scrub, how to use it and how often.

What does a body scrub do?

A body scrub is a physical exfoliator: small grains, such as sugar, coffee or fine plant powders, gently lift away dead skin cells as you massage. The result is skin that feels smoother and looks more even and fresh. It also makes the next step work better, because a moisturiser goes onto clean, smooth skin rather than a dry, flaky layer.

Which type of body scrub is right for you?

Cream body polish: gentle and quick

A cream polish mixes fine grains into a soft, creamy base, so it cleans and exfoliates at the same time and can replace your shower gel on scrub days. Vilvah Cookie N Cream Body Polish (£22.99, 200ml) combines coffee powder and ivory palm seed powder with shea butter, olive oil, argan oil and almond milk extract. It suits most skin types, including dry skin.

Powder scrubs: mix to the texture you like

Powder scrubs come dry; you mix a spoonful with water, rose water or toner into a paste. That makes them easy to adjust: a thicker paste for elbows and knees, a thinner one for softer skin. Deyga Body Scrub (£16.99, 100g) is a blend of dried fruit powders (lemon, papaya, pineapple, pomegranate and bitter orange) with purple rice. For something finer that also works on the face, Deyga Face & Body Exfoliator (£15.99, 50g) blends lemon, neem, matcha and black rice.

A luxury scrub in a jar

Highborn London Natural Luminosity Scrub (£50) is a natural exfoliant in a large 220ml glass jar, free from parabens and sulphates, in recyclable packaging. A good choice for a treat or a gift.

Tools: a loofah

Prefer to use your usual shower gel? A natural loofah such as the Deyga Organic Loofah (£12.99), made from plant fibres and biodegradable, adds gentle exfoliation to every wash.

Coffee body scrub: why it is so popular

A coffee body scrub is one of the most searched types in the UK. Ground coffee gives a satisfying, even texture and a warm, comforting smell that makes scrub day feel like a treat. Look for one in a creamy base with oils or butters, so skin does not feel tight afterwards; the Vilvah Cookie N Cream Body Polish is a good example. Rinse the shower tray afterwards so grounds do not build up in the drain.

How to use a body scrub, step by step

  1. Warm up. Shower or bathe for a few minutes first, so skin is warm and damp.
  2. Take a small amount, about a tablespoon for each arm or leg.
  3. Massage in slow circles with light pressure. Let the grains do the work; you do not need to press hard.
  4. Spend a little longer on rough areas, such as elbows, knees and heels.
  5. Rinse well with warm, not hot, water and pat skin dry.
  6. Moisturise straight away, while skin is still slightly damp.

How often should you use a body scrub?

For most people, once or twice a week is plenty. Dry or sensitive skin may prefer once a week, or a gentler cream polish. Scrubbing every day can leave skin feeling tight or tender, so more is not better. Skip the scrub on skin that is sunburnt, irritated, broken or freshly shaved or waxed; many people scrub the day before hair removal instead.

Body scrub for dry skin: what to use afterwards

If your skin is dry, the step after the scrub matters most. A rich butter locks in moisture on freshly exfoliated skin:

  • Deyga Chocolate Body Butter (£13.99, 100g): cocoa powder, cocoa butter and shea butter with almond and jojoba oils, and a light chocolate scent.

Scrub sets

Don't forget feet and lips

For feet, use Deyga Foot Scrub (£17.99) once a week, then Deyga Foot Butter (£12.99) before socks. Our foot cream guide walks through a full at-home pedicure. Good to know

  • Patch test first on a small area, especially if your skin is sensitive.

  • Keep water out of the jar and use dry hands to scoop, so the scrub stays fresh.

nodes.title: Body butter: how to choose it and how to use it
nodes.body:
When skin feels tight and dry, a body butter is the richest way to put comfort back. It is thicker than a lotion, melts on contact with warm skin and leaves a soft, cushioned finish. Here is how a body butter differs from a body lotion, which one suits your skin, and how to use it so a little goes a long way.

What is body butter?

A body butter is a thick, rich moisturiser for the body, made mainly from plant butters such as shea butter and cocoa butter. It feels firm in the jar, softens as it warms in your hands and leaves a soft, cushioned layer on the skin. A small amount covers a large area, so one jar lasts a good while.

Body butter vs body lotion: what is the difference?

The difference is mostly water. A body lotion is mainly water with some oils and butters, so it feels light, sinks in fast and suits everyday use. A body butter is made mostly or entirely of plant butters and oils, such as shea butter, cocoa butter and almond oil, so it is richer, takes a little longer to sink in and leaves skin feeling soft for longer. Body creams sit in between.

  • Choose a body butter for very dry or rough skin, for elbows, knees, shins and heels, at night, and in cold weather. Our winter skincare routine for dry skin puts it in a full routine.
  • Choose a body lotion for a quick morning routine, for warm days, or if you dislike a rich finish.

Many people use both: a lotion in the morning and a butter at night.

Our body butters, compared

Chocolate body butter

Deyga Chocolate Body Butter (£13.99, 100g) is a short, simple blend: cocoa powder, shea butter, almond oil, jojoba oil, cocoa butter and vitamin E, with no water in the ingredient list. The cocoa gives it a light, natural chocolate scent rather than a sweet perfume, which makes this chocolate body butter a favourite for evenings and a lovely small gift.

Rose and geranium body butter

Deyga Rose & Geranium Body Butter (£15.99, 40g) swaps cocoa for floral essential oils: rose and geranium with shea butter, almond oil, jojoba oil and vitamin E. The 40g size is small enough for a handbag, for dry hands and elbows on the go.

A luxury body butter

Highborn London Natural Luminosity Body Butter (£50) comes in a large 220ml glass jar in recyclable packaging, free from parabens and sulphates. Its butter-soft formula is made to smooth over the whole body, and the brand says it can be used on the face too.

Body butter for dry skin: how to use it

  1. Apply after a shower or bath, while skin is still slightly damp. The butter seals in the water on your skin. For the wash before it, see our body wash and bath bar guide.
  2. Warm a small amount, about the size of a grape for each leg, between your palms until it softens.
  3. Press, then smooth it over the skin in long strokes, rather than rubbing hard.
  4. Add a little more to elbows, knees, shins and heels.
  5. Give it a few minutes to sink in before getting dressed. At night, it can work while you sleep.

Once or twice a week, use a scrub first, such as Vilvah Cookie N Cream Body Polish (£22.99) or Deyga Body Scrub (£16.99). On freshly smoothed skin, a body butter spreads further and feels more even. Browse all body scrubs.

Prefer something lighter? Body lotions for dry skin

If a butter feels too rich, a body lotion for dry skin gives you the same ingredients in a lighter texture:

  • Deyga Almond Milk Body Lotion (£14.99, 100ml): almond milk, cocoa butter, shea butter and almond oil with cucumber water. A good pick if you are looking for a cocoa butter body lotion that is quick to absorb.
  • Vilvah Milk Body Lotion (£25.99, 250ml): oat milk, ceramides, olive squalane, coconut and jojoba oils in a vegan formula, made for daily use.

See all body lotions for dry skin, or shop more for dry skin.

Feet and lips

Heels and lips are the driest places of all, and they have their own butters. Deyga Foot Butter (£12.99, 40g) blends virgin coconut oil, olive oil, beeswax, vitamin E and vanilla essential oil; apply it at night and pull on cotton socks. Our foot cream guide has a simple at-home pedicure. For lips, Highborn London Superior Lip Butter (£22.50) comes in a 15ml size, or a large 50ml. For the softest lips, use a scrub first: see how to use a lip scrub.

Body butter and perfume

Perfume lasts longer on moisturised skin, because there is something for it to hold on to. Smooth an unscented or lightly scented butter over your pulse points before you spray. We explain how in how to layer oud with body butter.

Good to know

  • Patch test first, especially with butters that contain essential oils, such as rose, geranium or vanilla.
  • Keep it cool. Natural butters soften in warm rooms and firm up in the cold; keep the jar out of direct sun and heat.
  • Not for broken or irritated skin. If your skin is very dry, cracked or itchy for a long time, speak to a pharmacist or your GP.

nodes.title: Hair oils explained: amla, bhringraj, castor and how to oil your hair
nodes.body:
In India, oiling your hair is a weekly ritual passed down through families: warm oil massaged into the scalp, left to soak in, then washed out. It is one of the simplest ways to make dry hair feel softer and look glossier, and it is easy to start. Here is what the classic ingredients (amla, bhringraj, castor oil and more) bring to a hair oil, how to choose one, and how to oil your hair step by step.

What does a hair oil do?

A hair oil coats the hair shaft, so lengths feel softer, smoother and less frizzy, and look shinier. Used before washing, it cushions the lengths so they feel less dry after shampoo. And the scalp massage that goes with it is relaxing in itself. Think of a hair oil as a conditioning treatment for hair and scalp.

The key ingredients, explained

  • Amla (Indian gooseberry, Emblica officinalis) is the best-known ingredient in Ayurvedic hair care. In an amla hair oil, the dried fruit is steeped in a base oil such as coconut. Our Indian skincare guide covers amla and other Indian ingredients.
  • Bhringraj (Eclipta prostrata) is a herb traditionally used in Indian hair oils, often alongside amla. Bhringraj oil is usually a herbal infusion rather than a pure oil.
  • Castor oil is thick and rich. On its own it can feel heavy, so it works best mixed with lighter oils, which is how you will find it in most blends.
  • Coconut oil is the classic base for Indian hair oils, light enough for the scalp and rich enough for the lengths.
  • Hibiscus, fenugreek and curry leaf are kitchen-garden ingredients that often join amla in traditional blends.
  • Neem, tea tree and peppermint give an oil a fresh, cooling feel on the scalp.
  • Rosemary essential oil adds a herbal scent and is a popular addition to modern blends.

Our hair oils, compared

  • Deyga Hair Growth Oil (£14.99, 100ml): virgin coconut, almond, castor and sunflower oils infused with amla, bhringraj, hibiscus, fenugreek, curry leaves and other herbs, plus rosemary essential oil. A lightweight blend with an applicator tip for the scalp, and free from mineral oil and synthetic fragrance.
  • Vilvah Hair Growth Oil (£31.99, 200ml): pumpkin seed, black seed (kalonji), castor, grapeseed and almond oils with vitamin E, rosemary and peppermint. Alcohol-free and non-sticky.
  • Deyga Premature Greying Hair Oil (£18.99, 100ml): virgin coconut oil infused with amla, bhringraj, henna, bakuchi, moringa and liquorice, a classic Ayurvedic herbal blend.
  • Vilvah Anti-Dandruff Hair Oil (£19.99, 100ml): almond, neem and sesame oils with tea tree, peppermint, camphor, lemon and basil oils and amla oil, for a fresh, cooling scalp massage.
  • Deyga Neem Seed Oil (£14.99, 30ml): pure cold-pressed neem seed oil, a single ingredient. It has a strong natural smell, so most people mix a few drops into a lighter oil.

See every hair oil in one place.

A note on "hair growth" oils

Hair growth oil is one of the most searched hair care terms in the UK, and it is the name several brands give their blends (see them on our hair growth oil page). Be realistic about what any oil can do: it conditions hair and scalp, makes lengths feel softer and helps them look healthier. Hair loss has many causes, from genes to hormones, stress and diet, and no oil can change those. If you notice sudden, patchy or heavy hair loss, speak to your GP.

How to oil your hair, step by step

  1. Start with dry or slightly damp hair, before you wash it.
  2. Warm the oil. Stand the bottle in a bowl of warm water for a few minutes. Coconut-based oils turn solid in a cold bathroom; this melts them again.
  3. Part your hair into sections and apply a little oil along each parting with your fingertips or the applicator.
  4. Massage your scalp for 3 to 5 minutes with your fingertips in small circles, gently, without scratching.
  5. Smooth what is left through the lengths and ends, then comb through with a wide-tooth comb, such as a neem wood comb (£13.99).
  6. Leave it on for at least 30 minutes, or overnight with a towel over your pillow.
  7. Shampoo, and if hair still feels oily, shampoo a second time. Then condition the lengths.

Once or twice a week is plenty for most people.

Hair oil for dry hair

If your hair is dry, focus on the lengths and ends rather than the scalp, and choose a richer blend with coconut and castor oil. Our frizzy hair guide explains when to reach for an oil, a serum or a mask. Between washes, smooth a single drop over the ends to tame flyaways, or use a lighter leave-in such as Vilvah Anti-Frizz Hair Serum (£28.99). More ideas: hair oil for dry hair and hair serum for frizzy hair.

Washing it out

A gentle shampoo removes oil without leaving hair squeaky and dry. Try Deyga Rice Water Shampoo (from £10.99) or Vilvah Goat Milk Shampoo (£15.99, 250ml) with goat milk, jasmine and pea protein. If your scalp tends to flake, Vilvah Herbal Shampoo for Dandruff Control (from £12.99) pairs with the Anti-Dandruff Hair Oil; see all shampoos for dandruff. If flaking or itching does not settle, ask a pharmacist. For more on choosing a shampoo, read our natural shampoo guide.

Good to know

  • Patch test first, especially with oils that contain essential oils such as tea tree, peppermint, camphor or rosemary.
  • Keep oil away from your eyes, and do not use it on a broken, sore or irritated scalp.
  • Protect your pillow and clothes: oils can mark fabric.

nodes.title: Lip scrub: how to use one, and the lip balm to follow it
nodes.body:
Dry, flaky lips are one of the first things cold weather, central heating and long days in a mask or scarf leave behind. A lip scrub lifts the loose, flaky bits so your lips feel smooth again, and a good lip balm straight after keeps them soft. Here is how to use a lip scrub, how often, and which lip balm to pair with it.

What is a lip scrub?

A lip scrub is a small pot of fine sugar held in butters and oils. The sugar does the gentle polishing; the butters and oils leave a soft, cushioned layer behind. Ours are short, simple blends:

  • Deyga Mint Lip Scrub (£12.99, 16g): avocado and almond oils, beeswax, shea butter, granulated sugar, mint essential oil and vitamin E. Fresh and cooling to use.
  • Deyga Strawberry Lip Scrub (£10.99, 16g): the same base with strawberry essential oil for a fruity scent, free from artificial colours, alcohol and parabens.
  • Vilvah Natural Lip Scrub (£6.99, 10g): organic shea butter, avocado and almond oils, organic sugar, beeswax, and lemon and spearmint essential oils, free from alcohol and silicones. The small pot is easy to keep in a handbag.

How to use a lip scrub

  1. Start with clean, dry lips. Take off lipstick or balm first.
  2. Take a small amount, about the size of a grain of rice, on a clean fingertip.
  3. Massage in small circles for 30 seconds to a minute. Use light pressure: let the sugar do the work.
  4. Wipe or rinse it off with a soft, damp cloth or lukewarm water. Some people simply lick the sugar away.
  5. Apply a lip balm straight away, while lips are soft and smooth.

How often should you use a lip scrub?

For most people, two or three times a week is plenty. Lip skin is thin, so scrubbing every day can leave it feeling sore. In winter, or if your lips are very dry, use it when they feel flaky rather than on a fixed schedule. Before a matte or long-wear lipstick, a quick scrub helps the colour go on more evenly.

The lip balm to follow it

A scrub without a balm is only half the job. Choose the balm by what you want from it; our lip balm guide compares every type.

A natural lip balm for everyday

Deyga Beetroot Lip Balm Classic (from £10.99, 10g) blends beetroot extract with almond, avocado and jojoba oils, shea butter, beeswax and vitamin E. The beetroot gives lips a soft, natural flush. Deyga Natural Lip Balm (£9.99, 8g) is the plain choice: almond and jojoba oils, beeswax, shea butter and vanilla extract, in a light, non-greasy texture that sits well under lipstick.

A tinted lip balm

If you like a hint of colour, the Deyga Beetroot Lip Balm Stick (from £13.99, 5.5g) has the same beetroot blend in an easy tube. Vilvah Grape Fruit Lip Balm (£6.99) adds red iron oxide for a tint, with organic shea butter, avocado and almond oils and grapefruit essential oil. The Vilvah Tinted Lip Balm Kit (£17) brings two tinted balms together.

An SPF lip balm for daytime

Lips burn too, and most lip balms have no sun protection. Vilvah Milk Lip Balm SPF 30 PA+++ (£9.99) uses mineral filters, titanium dioxide and zinc oxide, with soy milk, soy butter, shea butter and kokum butter. Wear it outdoors and reapply as the pack directs, especially after eating or drinking.

A rich lip butter for night

Highborn London Superior Lip Butter (£22.50, 15ml) is a richer, softer texture to smooth on before bed after a scrub.

Lip scrub and balm sets

Sets pair a scrub with its balm, and make a neat small gift or stocking filler:

  • Deyga Soft Lip Combo (£17.99): Mint Lip Scrub and Beetroot Lip Balm.
  • Deyga Nourished Lip Care Kit (£25.99): Strawberry Lip Scrub and Beetroot Lip Balm.
  • Vilvah Lip Nourishing Kit (£13.99): Vilvah Lip Scrub and Grapefruit Lip Balm.

For more small gifts, see our Christmas gift guide or stocking fillers for her under £25.

Part of a wider routine

Lips are the driest skin of all, but the same idea works for the body: polish, then moisturise. Read how to choose a body scrub and how to use a body butter. Not sure which natural brand to start with? Compare them in Deyga or Vilvah.

Good to know

  • Patch test first, especially with scrubs and balms that contain essential oils such as mint, lemon or grapefruit.
  • Skip the scrub on cracked, cut, sore or sunburnt lips, or during a cold sore. Use only a balm until they have settled.
  • Lips that stay sore, split or swollen for a long time are worth showing to a pharmacist or your GP.
  • Keep pots clean: use a clean fingertip and close the lid after use.

nodes.title: Lattafa Khamrah Qahwa and Arabian perfume: a guide to the notes
nodes.body:
Few perfumes have travelled by word of mouth like Lattafa Khamrah Qahwa. It belongs to a wave of Arabian perfume houses, from Lattafa and Afnan to Al Haramain, Arabiyat Prestige and Maison Alhambra, whose rich, warm scents have found a big following in the UK. Here is what is in Khamrah Qahwa, what makes a perfume "Arabian", and how to choose one.

What does Lattafa Khamrah Qahwa smell like?

"Qahwa" is the Arabic word for coffee, and that is the idea at the heart of Lattafa Khamrah Qahwa Eau de Parfum (£26.99, 100ml). Its notes, from top to base:

  • Top: cinnamon, cardamom and ginger, the spices of Arabic coffee.
  • Heart: praline, candied fruits and white flowers.
  • Base: coffee, vanilla, tonka bean, benzoin and musk.

So it opens spicy, turns sweet and nutty, and settles into coffee and vanilla. It is an amber-woody, gourmand scent made for men and women, and it suits cooler months and evenings best.

More from Lattafa

Lattafa perfume is known for warm, generous scents at friendly prices. Alongside Khamrah Qahwa, we list:

  • Lattafa Teriaq (£29.99): caramel, bitter almond, pink pepper and apricot, then honey, rhubarb and rose over leather, vanilla and musk. Unisex.
  • Lattafa Maahir Black Edition (£25.99): black and pink pepper with saffron, then labdanum and cade oil over leather, cedarwood, guaiac wood and patchouli. A darker, smoky choice.
  • Lattafa Yara Candy (£26.99): green mandarin and blackcurrant, a strawberry-candy and gardenia heart, and vanilla, musk and sandalwood. Made for women.

See every Lattafa scent on the Lattafa page.

Afnan, Arabiyat Prestige and Maison Alhambra

Afnan 9am Dive (£26.99) is the fresh one: lemon, mint, pink pepper and blackcurrant, then apple, incense and cedarwood. Afnan Supremacy Gold (£27.99) is warmer, with nutmeg, violet and peach blossom over amber, vanilla, oud and benzoin. More on the Afnan page.

Arabiyat Prestige Nyla (£25.99, 80ml) is a bright floral-fruity scent for women: coconut, peach and mandarin, then tiare, jasmine and rose over white musk. See Arabiyat Prestige. Maison Alhambra adds a wide range of floral, fruity and woody eau de parfums at friendly prices.

What makes a perfume "Arabian"?

There is no strict rule, but Arabian perfume usually leans on a few ingredients:

  • Oud (agarwood): a deep, woody, slightly smoky note.
  • Amber and resins such as benzoin and labdanum: warm and sweet.
  • Saffron, cardamom and cinnamon: spice.
  • Rose and musk: soft and rounded.

Most of the scents above are eau de parfum, which typically holds around 15–20% perfume oil. Read extrait vs eau de parfum for what each label means.

Arabian perfume in stock now

Warm and spicy

Al Haramain Amber Oud Tobacco Edition (£32.99, 60ml) shares Khamrah Qahwa's love of spice: tobacco leaf, cinnamon, black pepper and ginger, then vanilla, clove, star anise, cacao and tonka bean. Al Haramain Amber Oud Black Edition (£39.99) pairs cardamom and lavender with leather, amber and benzoin.

Sweet and fruity

Al Haramain Amber Oud Gold Edition (from £32.99) is bergamot, melon and pineapple over vanilla and musk, a popular first Arabian perfume. Al Haramain Amber Oud Ruby Edition (from £41.99) mixes saffron and bitter almond with jasmine and ambergris. Al Haramain Amber Musk (£39.99) is softer: amber, musk, vanilla and resins.

Oud and saffron

Fumeri Oud Saffron (£29.99) and SAP Saffron Oud Extrait de Parfum (£43.99) both open on saffron and spice before oud, cedarwood and smoky woods, with amber, leather and musk. Montale Aoud Safran (£62.99) builds on saffron and oud with rose and amber.

Every Al Haramain Amber Oud edition is compared in our Amber Oud guide. Browse all Arabian perfume and oud perfume. For designer ouds such as Tom Ford Oud Wood and Gucci Intense Oud, read our oud perfume guide.

How to wear a rich, warm perfume

  • Start small: one or two sprays on the neck or wrists. You can add more; you cannot take it away.
  • Spray on moisturised skin, so the scent has something to sit on. We explain how in how to layer oud with body butter.
  • Try it on skin before you decide. Warm notes change over the first hour, so judge the base, not just the first spray.
  • Patch test if your skin is sensitive to fragrance.

Arabian perfume also makes a generous gift: see our Christmas gift guide.

nodes.title: Dior Sauvage EDT vs EDP vs Parfum: which one to choose
nodes.body:
Dior Sauvage is one of the best-known men's fragrances in the UK, and it comes in more than one strength. The eau de toilette, the eau de parfum and the parfum share a name and a bottle shape, but they are not the same scent at different volumes. Here is what each label means, what is in the Dior Sauvage eau de parfum, and how to choose.

EDT, EDP and Parfum: what the labels mean

The label tells you how much perfume oil is in the bottle. The ranges below are typical; every house sets its own.

  • Eau de toilette (EDT): typically around 5–15% perfume oil. Lighter, with a bright opening that suits daytime and warm weather.
  • Eau de parfum (EDP): usually around 15–20%. Fuller and rounder, and the most popular strength today.
  • Parfum (also called extrait): the most concentrated form, typically around 20–40%. Richer and closer to the skin, so a little goes further.

A higher concentration does not simply mean "stronger". Perfumers often rework the formula for each strength, so the notes, the balance and the feel on skin change too. We explain this in more detail in extrait vs eau de parfum: what the label means.

Dior Sauvage eau de parfum: the notes

Sauvage EDP is an amber fougère inspired by the desert at sundown, mixing fresh, spicy and warm notes:

  • Top: Calabrian bergamot and Sichuan pepper.
  • Heart: star anise, nutmeg and lavender.
  • Base: Papua New Guinea vanilla and ambroxan.

Compared with an eau de toilette, an EDP like this tends to feel softer and warmer, with the vanilla and amber showing more as it settles. It works year-round, and especially in the evening and in cooler months.

Sauvage eau de toilette

The EDT is the lighter, brighter version and the one many people try first. You can try it in miniature in the Dior Iconics Mini Perfume Discovery Set (£92.99), which holds five 5ml Dior scents: Sauvage Eau de Toilette, J'adore Eau de Parfum, Hypnotic Poison Eau de Toilette, and Miss Dior in both Eau de Parfum and Eau de Toilette. It is a good way to compare styles before choosing a full bottle, and a generous gift.

Sauvage Parfum

Dior Sauvage Parfum is the most concentrated of the three and is usually described as the richest and warmest. We do not carry the Parfum at present, so if you have your heart set on it, get in touch and we will let you know if that changes.

Which Dior Sauvage should you choose?

  • Choose the EDT if you want something fresh for daytime, the office or summer.
  • Choose the EDP if you want a softer, warmer version for every day and evenings.
  • Choose the Parfum if you prefer a rich scent that sits close to the skin.
  • Not sure? Try a mini first, then buy the full size.

The Dior Sauvage gift set

The Dior Sauvage Eau de Parfum 100ml + 10ml Men's Gift Set (£144) pairs a full 100ml bottle with a 10ml travel spray, so there is one for home and one for the gym bag or a trip. See more gift ideas in our Christmas gift guide.

More fresh, aromatic men's fragrances

If you like Sauvage's mix of citrus, pepper and lavender, these share some of those notes, each in its own style:

  • Calvin Klein Eternity for Men Eau de Toilette (£38.99, 100ml): mandarin, lavender, bergamot and lemon, then sage, juniper and basil over sandalwood and vetiver.
  • Calvin Klein Defy Parfum (from £22.99): mandarin and pink pepper, lavender and a suede accord, then vetiver, amber and woods.
  • Al Haramain Amber Oud Carbon Edition (from £35.99): lavender, rosemary and bergamot, then sage, cedarwood and geranium over vetiver and amber.
  • Al Haramain Amber Oud Black Edition (£39.99): cardamom, grapefruit and lavender with leather, amber and benzoin.
  • Al Haramain L'Aventure (£29.99): lemon, bergamot and elemi over patchouli, amber and musk.
  • Armaf Hunter (£19.99): grapefruit, mandarin, rosemary and cardamom over cedarwood, vetiver and musk.

Like Eternity for Men? Compare it with the women's version in Calvin Klein Eternity for women vs for men.

How to wear it

  • Two to four sprays of an EDT, one to three of an EDP, and one or two of a parfum is a good starting point.
  • Spray on moisturised skin at the neck and chest. There is no need to rub it in.
  • Keep the bottle cool and out of direct sunlight, not on a bathroom windowsill.

nodes.title: Calvin Klein Eternity for women vs for men: the difference explained
nodes.body:
Calvin Klein Eternity is a name shared by two classic fragrances: Eternity for women and Eternity for men. They sit side by side on the shelf, in similar clean, simple bottles, but they smell quite different. Here is what is in each one, how the strengths compare, and how to choose, whether for yourself or as a gift.

Calvin Klein Eternity for women

Calvin Klein Eternity Eau de Parfum (from £28.99, 30ml or 100ml) is a classic floral: fresh citrus at the start, a big bouquet of white and spring flowers in the middle, and a soft woody base.

  • Top: freesia, mandarin orange, sage and citrus.
  • Heart: lily, carnation, violet, jasmine, rose, lily of the valley, marigold and narcissus.
  • Base: sandalwood, amber, musk, heliotrope and patchouli.

It is graceful, clean and easy to wear: a good everyday scent for the office, weddings and special days alike.

Calvin Klein Eternity for men

Calvin Klein Eternity for Men Eau de Toilette (£38.99, 100ml) is a fresh aromatic fragrance: citrus and lavender first, then herbs, then warm woods.

  • Top: mandarin orange, lavender, bergamot and lemon.
  • Heart: sage, juniper berries, basil, geranium, jasmine and coriander.
  • Base: sandalwood, vetiver, musk, amber and Brazilian rosewood.

It feels crisp and clean, with a warm finish, and suits daytime and work as well as evenings.

Eternity for women vs for men: the key differences

  • Character: the women's Eternity is floral, built around lily, carnation and rose. The men's is aromatic, built around lavender and herbs such as sage, juniper and basil.
  • What they share: mandarin and sage near the top, and sandalwood, amber and musk in the base. That is why they feel like a pair.
  • Strength: we stock the women's Eternity as an eau de parfum and the men's as an eau de toilette. An eau de parfum typically holds around 15–20% perfume oil and an eau de toilette around 5–15%, so the women's feels a little fuller on skin. Read what the labels mean.
  • Who can wear them: anyone. Many women enjoy the men's lavender freshness, and many men like the women's soft florals. Choose by the notes you love.

The newer Eternity scents, in miniature

Calvin Klein has added deeper versions of Eternity. Our 10ml minis are an easy way to try them:

  • Calvin Klein Eternity Parfum for men (£18.99, 10ml): lavender and rum, warm spices and aromatic notes, then vanilla, woods and amber. Deeper and warmer than the classic men's EDT.
  • Eternity Aromatic Essence Parfum Intense for men (£18.99, 10ml): juniper berry and fresh aromatic notes, lavender and a coconut accord, then cardamom, woods and amber.
  • Eternity Aromatic Essence Parfum Intense for women (£18.99, 10ml): lavender and fresh aromatic notes, a floral and coconut heart, then amber, woods and musk.

See all our travel-size minis.

Eternity as a gift

For her, the Calvin Klein Women's Miniature Fragrance Set (£33.99) holds four 15ml bottles: Eternity Eau de Parfum, CK One Eau de Toilette and two Obsession Eau de Parfum, so she can try three classic styles. For him, pair the Eternity for Men EDT with the Eternity Parfum mini for travel. More ideas in our Christmas gift guide.

If you like Eternity, try

  • Calvin Klein Defy Parfum (from £22.99): mandarin, pink pepper, lavender and a suede accord over vetiver, amber and woods. A modern pick for Eternity for Men fans who like lavender.
  • Calvin Klein My Euphoria Eau de Parfum (£18.99, 10ml): a floral gourmand mini for women who want something sweeter than Eternity's clean florals.

Another men's classic that comes in more than one strength: Dior Sauvage EDT vs EDP vs Parfum.

How to wear it

  • Spray on moisturised skin at the neck and chest; scent has more to hold on to. See how to use a body butter.
  • Two or three sprays of eau de toilette, or one or two of eau de parfum or parfum, is a good start.
  • Keep the bottle cool and out of sunlight.

nodes.title: Face wash for your skin type: dry, oily and sensitive skin
nodes.body:
A good cleanse is the first step of every skincare routine, and the wrong face wash can undo the rest. Too harsh, and skin feels tight and dry; too rich, and oily skin feels heavy. Here is how to choose a face wash for your skin type, what the different textures and ingredients mean, and how to cleanse.

First, know your skin type

Wash with a mild cleanser, pat dry and wait about an hour without applying anything. Then look and feel:

  • Dry: feels tight, and may look flaky or dull.
  • Oily: looks shiny all over, especially on the forehead, nose and chin.
  • Combination: shiny in the centre, normal or dry on the cheeks.
  • Sensitive: easily stings, turns red or reacts to fragrance.

Face wash for dry skin

Dry skin needs a cleanser that lifts away the day without stripping. Look for creamy or milky textures and soothing, moisture-loving ingredients. For a full cold-weather routine, see our winter skincare routine for dry skin.

Deyga Oat Milk Face Wash (£12.99, 100ml) combines oat milk with provitamin B5, kaolin and mild cleansers made from coconut and corn. Deyga makes it for dry, sensitive and normal skin. Vilvah Fragrance-Free Cream Face Wash (£9.99, 100ml) is a soft cream with banana fruit extract, hydrolysed wheat protein and glycerine. Shop every face wash for dry skin.

Face wash for sensitive skin

If your skin reacts easily, keep the ingredient list short and skip added fragrance. The Vilvah Fragrance-Free Cream Face Wash is made without fragrance, and Vilvah describes it as pH-balanced. The Deyga Oat Milk Face Wash is mild too, but it does contain fragrance, so patch test it first. See more for sensitive skin.

Face wash for oily skin

Oily skin likes a foaming or gel wash that leaves skin feeling fresh but not squeaky. Over-washing can make skin feel tighter without making it any less shiny, so twice a day is enough.

  • Vilvah Honey Face Wash (£12.99, 100ml): 10% raw honey with papaya and blackberry extracts, witch hazel and gotu kola, and a citrus-vanilla scent. Vilvah makes it for normal to oily skin, with a medium foam.
  • Vilvah Milk Powder Face Wash (£13.99, 50g): a water-free powder that turns to foam in wet hands, with rice powder, rice milk extract, oat flour, hyaluronic acid and papain, a papaya enzyme. Fragrance-free and made for normal to oily skin.

Shop every face wash for oily skin and more for oily skin.

Tea tree, charcoal and vitamin C face washes

Tea tree and charcoal

Deyga Charcoal Face Wash (from £12.99, 100ml) is a gel built on tea tree hydrosol, with activated charcoal from coconut shell and gentle coconut and corn-based cleansers. It is a popular pick if you are looking for a tea tree face wash: fresh-feeling, and made for all skin types.

Vitamin C

Deyga Vitamin C Foaming Face Wash (£15.99, 100ml) uses ascorbyl glucoside, a stable form of vitamin C, with citron, bitter orange and lemon hydrosols in a light foam. A bright, zesty wash for the morning.

Cream, foam or powder?

  • Cream and milk washes feel the softest: good for dry and sensitive skin.
  • Foams and gels feel fresh and light: good for oily and combination skin. Shiseido Complete Cleansing Microfoam (£29.99, 180ml) is a fine, lightweight foam for everyday use.
  • Powders are mixed with water as you use them, and travel well.
  • A luxury cleanser: Highborn London Crystal Cleanser (£24, 100ml) contains co-enzyme Q10 and is made for morning and night.

How to wash your face

  1. Wet your face with lukewarm water, not hot.
  2. Use a small amount, about the size of a 5p coin, and work it into a lather in your hands.
  3. Massage gently for 30 to 60 seconds, including the hairline and jaw. Keep it away from your eyes.
  4. Rinse well and pat dry with a clean towel.
  5. Follow straight away with toner or moisturiser while skin is still slightly damp.

Most people do best washing twice a day: morning and night. If you wear make-up or sunscreen, cleanse twice at night: once to lift it, once to clean the skin.

After cleansing

A cleanser is only the first step. Add a toner if you like one (see how to choose a toner), then a moisturiser: see our moisturisers for dry skin, or read moisturiser for your skin type. Once or twice a week, add a mask: see our face mask guide. Light, soothing layers such as aloe vera gel suit oily skin; read how to use aloe vera gel. Not sure which natural brand suits you? Compare them in Deyga or Vilvah.

Good to know

  • Patch test any new face wash on your jaw or inner arm first.
  • Change one thing at a time, so you know what suits you.
  • Breakouts, redness or itching that last are worth showing to a pharmacist or your GP.

nodes.title: Natural shampoo: how to choose one for dry hair, frizz and a flaky scalp
nodes.body:
More people are switching to a natural shampoo: one built on plant-derived cleansers, with milks, waters and botanical extracts in place of a long list of synthetics. But "natural" is not a legal term in the UK, so the label alone tells you little. Here is how to read a shampoo, which one suits dry hair, frizz or a flaky scalp, and the conditioner or hair mask to follow it with.

What makes a shampoo "natural"?

Every shampoo needs a cleanser to lift oil and dirt. In the shampoos below, most come from coconut, corn or sugar beet: names such as decyl glucoside, coco-glucoside, sodium cocoyl isethionate and cocamidopropyl betaine. Around them sit the ingredients that give each shampoo its character, such as rice water, goat milk, rosemary or neem. Always read the full ingredient list on the product page: it tells you far more than the word "natural" on the front.

Shampoo for dry hair

Dry hair needs a cleanse that leaves moisture behind. Look for a creamy shampoo with milks, proteins or oils.

  • Vilvah Goat Milk Shampoo (£15.99, 250ml): goat milk and jasmine flower water with hydrolysed keratin, pea protein, panthenol and jojoba oil, in a creamy lather. Vilvah makes it for dry, frizzy or chemically treated hair. Our goat milk soap guide covers Vilvah’s other goat milk products.
  • Deyga Rice Water Shampoo (from £10.99, 50ml or 220ml): rice water with coconut- and corn-derived cleansers. A light, everyday shampoo for all hair types.

Rice water shampoo

Rice water has long been used in Asian hair care, where people rinsed their hair with the water left from soaking rice. A rice water shampoo puts that into an easy, everyday cleanser; the Deyga one leads its ingredient list with rice water and leaves hair feeling soft and smooth.

Shampoo for a flaky scalp

Scalp shampoos use herbal ingredients with a fresh, clean feel:

  • Vilvah Herbal Shampoo for Dandruff Control (from £12.99): neem leaf, tea tree and black pepper oils, rosemary and basil waters and amla, made without parabens.
  • Deyga Anti Dandruff Shampoo (£14.99, 220ml): rosemary leaf hydrosol, ginger extract and a yeast ferment extract, with mild cleansers. Deyga makes it for frequent use and says it is safe for colour-treated hair.

Massage it into the scalp, not just the lengths, and leave it for a minute before rinsing. Flakes, itching or redness that do not settle are worth showing to a pharmacist or your GP. Shop every shampoo for dandruff, or see our dandruff care edit.

Conditioner for dry hair

Conditioner smooths the hair after shampoo, so it detangles easily and feels softer.

  • Vilvah Cream Conditioner (£15.99, 250ml): tucuma butter, broccoli seed oil, aloe vera, jasmine and pea protein. Vilvah says it can also be left on for up to 15 minutes as a mask.
  • Deyga Soy Milk Conditioner (£11.99, 50ml): soybean extract, argan oil, provitamin B5 and vitamin E in a lightweight texture.

Hair mask for dry hair

Once a week, swap your conditioner for a mask. Vilvah Goat Milk Hair Mask (£31.99, 200g) combines goat milk with ceramides, argan oil, vitamin E and a seaweed extract. Apply it to clean, damp lengths, leave it for 10 to 15 minutes, then rinse. Vilvah says it also works as a leave-in styling aid for curls. See every hair mask for dry hair.

How to wash your hair

  1. Wet your hair thoroughly with warm, not hot, water.
  2. Use a coin-sized amount of shampoo, more for long or thick hair.
  3. Focus on the scalp, massaging with your fingertips, not your nails. The lather will clean the lengths as you rinse.
  4. Rinse well, then apply conditioner to the mid-lengths and ends.
  5. Leave it for a minute or two, comb through with a wide-tooth comb, and rinse.
  6. Pat dry with a towel rather than rubbing, which can rough up the hair.

How often? Dry or curly hair often does well with two or three washes a week; an oily scalp may prefer every other day. Natural shampoos can lather less than you are used to, so a second, smaller wash is fine.

Before and after the wash

Oiling before a wash is a long tradition in Indian hair care: read our guide to hair oils. For a full frizz routine, see frizzy hair: serum, oil or mask. For frizz after drying, a few drops of serum help smooth flyaways; the Vilvah Shampoo & Hair Serum Kit (£25.99) pairs the Goat Milk Shampoo with the Anti-Frizz Hair Serum. See all hair serums for frizzy hair.

Good to know

  • Patch test a new shampoo behind the ear, especially one with essential oils such as tea tree or rosemary.
  • Keep it out of your eyes; rinse with water if it gets in.
  • Switching brands? Give your hair two or three weeks to settle before you judge.

nodes.title: Moisturiser for your skin type: dry, oily, sensitive and combination
nodes.body:
A good moisturiser is the step that holds the rest of your routine together. It softens skin, helps it feel comfortable all day and gives make-up or sunscreen a smooth base. But the right texture depends on your skin: a rich cream that rescues dry skin can feel heavy on oily skin, and a light lotion may not be enough in winter. Here is how to choose a moisturiser for your skin type.

Cream, lotion or gel: what is the difference?

Most moisturisers mix water with oils and butters. The more oil and butter, the richer the texture:

  • Rich creams hold more butters and oils, such as shea butter and almond oil. They suit dry and very dry skin, and cold weather.
  • Light creams and lotions have more water and lighter oils. They suit normal, oily and combination skin.
  • Gels and serums are mostly water with moisture-loving ingredients such as glycerine and hyaluronic acid. They work on their own for oily skin, or under a cream.

Moisturiser for dry skin

Dry skin feels tight, may flake and drinks a light lotion straight in. Look for a cream with butters and oils. When the weather turns cold, see our winter skincare routine for dry skin.

Deyga Deep Moisturising Face Cream (£18.99, 30g) blends shea butter with marula and almond oils, centella asiatica (gotu kola) and cardamom, and Deyga makes it without artificial fragrance. Highborn London Imperial Moisturiser (£46, 50ml) is a richer, nourishing cream made in England for dry, tight-feeling skin. See more moisturisers for dry skin.

Moisturiser for oily skin

Oily skin still needs moisture: skipping it can leave skin feeling tight while it still looks shiny. Choose a light, fast-absorbing texture.

Deyga Light Moisturising Face Cream (£18.99, 30g) is made for oily and normal skin, with rosehip, almond and avocado oils, shea butter, centella asiatica and ectoin, and a hint of vanilla essential oil. On very oily days, a serum such as Deyga 2% Hyaluronic Acid Serum (£22.99, 20ml) can be enough on its own. More ideas for oily skin.

Moisturiser for sensitive skin

Sensitive skin does best with a short ingredient list and no added fragrance. Of the creams above, the Deyga Deep Moisturising Face Cream is made without artificial fragrance; the Light cream contains vanilla essential oil, so patch test it first. Introduce one new product at a time, and see more for sensitive skin.

Moisturiser for combination skin

Combination skin is oily through the centre and normal or dry on the cheeks. Use a light moisturiser all over and add a little richer cream only where skin feels dry. Vilvah Ultra Moisturising Cream (£25.99, 50ml) is a good middle ground: olive squalane, glycerine and plant extracts in a non-greasy cream that Vilvah makes for all skin types, with white lily essential oil.

Add a hydrating serum underneath

Serums are light and watery, so they go on before your moisturiser. A hyaluronic acid serum such as the Deyga 2% Hyaluronic Acid Serum (sodium hyaluronate, panthenol, aloe and centella) or Vilvah Milk Drops Hydrating Serum (from £21.99), with aloe vera juice, hyaluronic acid and rice milk extract, adds a layer of moisture that the cream then seals in. Aloe vera gel works in a similar way; read how to use aloe vera gel. Browse every serum, or read our face serum guide.

Day cream or night cream?

By day, your moisturiser sits under sunscreen and make-up, so a lighter texture often works best. Finish with SPF, or use a moisturiser with SPF built in, such as Highborn London GLOWGUARD SPF30 Moisturiser (from £49), which uses non-nano zinc oxide.

At night there is no sunscreen or make-up to layer, so many people like something richer. A night cream such as Highborn London Night Elixir (from £26) is a comforting cream made for the last step of an evening routine. The Ultimate Day & Night Moisture Set (£95) pairs it with the Imperial Moisturiser.

How to apply moisturiser

  1. Cleanse with a face wash that suits your skin: see face wash for your skin type.
  2. Apply serum, if you use one, to slightly damp skin. A toner after cleansing gives that first damp layer: see toner for dry skin.
  3. Warm a pea-sized amount of moisturiser between your fingertips.
  4. Press and smooth it over your face and neck with upward strokes, avoiding the eyes. For the eye area, see our under eye cream guide.
  5. In the morning, finish with sunscreen unless your moisturiser has SPF.

What makes a moisturiser "natural"?

There is no legal definition of "natural" in the UK, so read the ingredient list rather than the label. In the creams above you will find plant butters and oils (shea, marula, rosehip, avocado, almond, olive squalane) alongside glycerine, water and an emulsifier that keeps them blended. Full ingredient lists are on every product page.

Good to know

  • Patch test a new moisturiser on your jaw or inner arm for 24 hours.
  • Your skin changes with the seasons: many people switch to a richer cream in winter and a lighter one in summer.
  • Dryness, redness or itching that lasts is worth showing to a pharmacist or your GP.

Explore every product for hydration, our Highborn London range and the full skincare shelf, all dispatched from the UK.

nodes.title: Face masks: clay, charcoal and face packs, and how to use them
nodes.body:
A face mask is the easiest way to give your skin ten minutes of extra care. Once or twice a week, it can leave skin feeling fresher, softer or more comfortable, depending on the type you choose. Here are the main kinds of face mask, which suits your skin, and how to use one.

The main types of face mask

  • Clay masks use clays such as kaolin or French pink clay. They dry down on the skin and feel deep-cleansing, which makes them popular with oily and combination skin.
  • Charcoal masks add activated charcoal, often with tea tree, for a fresh, clarifying feel.
  • Powder face packs are dry blends of plant powders that you mix with water, rose water or aloe gel just before use.
  • Cream and gel masks are hydrating and stay soft on the skin, which suits dry and tired-looking skin.

Clay face masks

Vilvah Milk Mud Mask (£19.99, 50ml) is a creamy clay face mask: kaolin clay with oat milk extract, saffron extract and liquorice root extract, made without sulphates, silicones or artificial fragrance, and suitable for all skin types including sensitive skin. Vilvah Wild Rose Face Mask (£11.99, 100ml) keeps things short and simple: aloe vera, French pink clay and rose hydrosol. Vilvah suggests using it two or three times a week.

Charcoal face masks

Deyga Charcoal Detox Face Mask (£13.99, 100g) combines activated charcoal with tea tree and jasmine hydrosols, and is made without parabens or artificial fragrance. Vilvah Charcoal Face Mask (£12.99, 100ml) pairs charcoal with aloe vera and tea tree hydrosol. Both have a fresh, clean feel that many people with oily skin enjoy. See more face masks for oily skin.

Powder face packs

Face packs are a long-standing part of Indian skincare: dried herbs, fruit peels and clays ground to a powder and mixed fresh each time.

  • Deyga Orange & Almond Face Pack (£19.99, 100g): sun-dried orange pulp and zest, almond meal and turmeric. The almond meal gives it a gentle, polishing texture.
  • Deyga Spirulina Matcha Face Pack (£17.99, 150g): spirulina, matcha, neem, moringa and aloe vera powder, for a green, earthy mask.

Mix a teaspoon with water, or with Deyga Pure Rose Water Toner (£11.99) for a softer scent, into a smooth paste. You may know the classic Indian clay multani mitti (Fuller's earth) used the same way; kaolin and French pink clay are other clays used in face masks.

Hydrating masks and eye masks

For skin that feels dry or tired rather than oily, choose a cream or gel mask that stays soft. The 24K Gold Hydrating Face Mask (£34.99) combines 24K gold with hyaluronic acid, ceramides, shea butter and centella asiatica, and makes a lovely treat or gift. For the delicate eye area, Deyga Under Eye Mask (£15.99, 15g) is a balm of kalonji, hemp seed, almond, rosehip and carrot seed oils with beeswax, to dab on at night. For eye creams and gels, read our under eye cream guide.

Which face mask suits your skin?

  • Oily or combination skin: clay or charcoal masks, on the T-zone or the whole face.
  • Dry skin: a hydrating cream mask, or a creamy clay mask such as the Milk Mud Mask, rinsed off before it dries completely.
  • Sensitive skin: a short ingredient list without added fragrance, and a patch test first.
  • Not sure? Try multi-masking: clay on the oily areas, a hydrating mask on the dry ones.

How to use a face mask

  1. Cleanse first with a face wash that suits your skin: see face wash for your skin type.
  2. Apply an even layer with clean fingertips or a brush, avoiding the eyes and lips.
  3. Leave it on for the time on the pack, usually 10 to 15 minutes. Rinse clay masks before they crack and pull, so skin does not feel tight.
  4. Rinse with lukewarm water and a soft cloth, then pat dry.
  5. Follow with toner and moisturiser straight away. Aloe vera gel is a light option: read how to use aloe vera gel.

How often should you use a face mask?

For most people, clay and charcoal masks once or twice a week are plenty; dry or sensitive skin may prefer once a week. Hydrating masks can be used more often. Always follow the directions on the pack.

Good to know

  • Patch test any new mask on your jaw or inner arm first.
  • Turmeric can leave a faint yellow tint on skin and towels; rinse well and use an old towel.
  • Skip masks on broken, sunburnt or irritated skin. Breakouts or redness that last are worth showing to a pharmacist or your GP.

nodes.title: Oud perfume: Tom Ford Oud Wood, Gucci Intense Oud and other oud fragrances
nodes.body:
Oud is one of the most talked-about notes in perfume: deep, woody and a little smoky. Designer houses such as Tom Ford, Gucci, Guerlain and Chopard each have their own take on it. Here is what oud is, how the best-known oud perfumes differ, and how to choose and wear one.

What is oud?

Oud, also called agarwood or aoud, is a dark, fragrant resin that forms in the wood of agar (Aquilaria) trees. It has been treasured in the Middle East and South Asia for centuries, burned as incense and worn as an oil. Natural oud is rare, so many modern perfumes use an oud accord: a blend of woods, resins and leathery notes built to give the same rich effect. Gucci, for example, lists an oud accord in its base notes.

Tom Ford Oud Wood

Tom Ford Oud Wood Eau de Parfum (from £115.99, 30ml or 50ml) is the gentlest way into oud. Its key notes are oud wood, rosewood and cardamom over sandalwood, vetiver, tonka bean and amber, so the oud reads smooth and warm rather than smoky. It is unisex and easy to wear in the office or in the evening. See every Tom Ford fragrance, or read our Tom Ford perfume guide for Black Orchid, Noir Extreme and Neroli Portofino.

Gucci Intense Oud

Gucci Intense Oud Eau de Parfum (£73.99, 90ml) is darker. Black pepper and olibanum (frankincense) open it; amber woods, sandalwood and cedarwood sit at the heart; leather, patchouli, gurjun balsam and the oud accord form the base. Expect incense and leather more than sweetness. Shop all Gucci, or compare it with Bloom, Flora Gorgeous and Guilty in our Gucci perfume guide.

Tom Ford Oud Wood or Gucci Intense Oud?

  • Choose Oud Wood if you want a soft, creamy wood with a touch of spice that suits everyday wear.
  • Choose Intense Oud if you like incense, leather and a bolder, smokier trail for evenings and colder months.

Three more oud perfumes

  • Guerlain Oud Essentiel (£94.99, 125ml): saffron and pelargonium, then rose, oud and cedarwood over leather, frankincense and guaiac wood. A rose-and-leather oud, made unisex.
  • Chopard Oud Malaki (£48.99, 80ml): grapefruit, lavender and artemisia, then tobacco, spices and leather over oud, ambergris and dark woods. Made for men, and the most affordable oud in this guide.
  • Montale Aoud Damascus (£52.99, 100ml): damask rose, aoud and saffron with amber, woods and musk. Montale is known for rose and oud, and this one is made for women.

The Al Haramain Amber Oud editions

Al Haramain's Amber Oud range is a popular Arabian line, but read the notes: not every edition is built around oud. Our Amber Oud editions guide compares them all. Amber Oud White Edition (from £34.99) is bergamot and orange, then jasmine, rose and freesia over musk, vanilla and patchouli, and is listed for women. Amber Oud Carbon Edition (from £35.99) is a fresh, aromatic men's scent of lavender, rosemary, bergamot, sage and vetiver. Amber Oud Bleu Edition (from £38.99) is citrus and mint over incense, vetiver and sandalwood. For the Gold, Ruby, Tobacco and Black editions, and for Lattafa, read our guide to Arabian perfume and Lattafa Khamrah Qahwa.

Which oud perfume suits you?

  • New to oud: Tom Ford Oud Wood, or a fresher Amber Oud edition.
  • You love incense and leather: Gucci Intense Oud or Guerlain Oud Essentiel.
  • You love rose: Montale Aoud Damascus or Guerlain Oud Essentiel.
  • Warm and spicy: Chopard Oud Malaki.

Oud is traditionally unisex, so "for men" or "for women" on the label is only a starting point. Browse unisex perfume, perfume for men and perfume for women.

How to wear oud

  1. Start small: one or two sprays. Oud notes are rich, and a little goes a long way.
  2. Apply to moisturised skin on the wrists, neck or chest. Our guide to layering oud with body butter explains why.
  3. Let it settle: do not rub your wrists together. Oud perfumes often change a lot after the first half hour, so judge them later in the day.
  4. Test before you buy a full bottle if you can, or start with a smaller size.

Good to know

  • Eau de parfum is the most common strength for oud perfumes; read extrait vs eau de parfum for what the label means.
  • Patch test on your inner arm if you have sensitive skin, and keep perfume away from your eyes.
  • Store bottles away from heat and sunlight, with the cap on.

nodes.title: Under eye cream: how to choose one and how to apply it
nodes.body:
The skin around your eyes is thinner than the rest of your face, and it moves every time you blink, smile or squint. That is why many people give it its own product. An under eye cream is a small, gentle moisturiser made for this delicate area. Here is how to choose one, how to apply it, and what to expect.

Do you need an eye cream?

You can use your face moisturiser around the eyes, as long as it does not sting. An eye cream is worth it if your moisturiser feels too rich or makes your eyes water, if the area feels dry or tight, or if you simply enjoy a separate step. Eye creams come in small jars, have a texture made for patting on, and are usually made without added fragrance.

Cream, gel or balm?

  • Light creams suit most skin and sit well under make-up.
  • Gels feel cool and weightless, and suit oily skin or a morning routine.
  • Balms and oils are richer, and suit dry skin or a night routine.

Under eye creams to try

Deyga Under Eye Cream (from £14.99, 15g) is a light, cooling cream of aloe vera, cucumber hydrosol, almond oil, potato starch and vitamin E. Deyga makes it without silicones, parabens or artificial fragrance, and it can sit under make-up. Vilvah Natural Under Eye Cream (£19.99, 20ml) is a little richer: glycerine, witch hazel, shea butter and sunflower seed oil with bamboo, goji berry and cardamom extracts, made without alcohol or silicones.

For a gel, Highborn London Imperial Eye Gel (from £31, 10ml, 15ml or 30ml) gives lightweight moisture with a cooling feel: glycerin and a form of hyaluronic acid with argan, avocado and sunflower oils. It contains fragrance, so patch test it if your skin is sensitive. See every eye cream.

An eye balm for night

Deyga Under Eye Mask (£15.99, 15g) is a rich balm rather than a sheet mask: kalonji (black seed), hemp seed, almond, rosehip and carrot seed oils with beeswax. Dab a little on before bed, when there is no make-up to layer on top.

What about dark circles?

Dark circles have many causes, from the shape of the face and the shadows it casts to genes, tiredness and allergies. An eye cream keeps the skin moisturised and comfortable, and a cool, light texture can make tired-looking eyes feel fresher, but no cream can promise to remove dark circles. Sleep, sunscreen and a little concealer often help more. If the area suddenly darkens, swells or itches, ask a pharmacist or your GP.

How to apply eye cream

  1. Cleanse and tone first. A gentle toner such as Deyga Pure Rose Water Toner (£11.99) keeps the routine simple; read our guide to face wash for your skin type.
  2. Take a rice-grain amount for both eyes. More is not better here.
  3. Use your ring finger, which has the lightest touch, and dot the cream along the orbital bone, below the eye and under the brow.
  4. Pat, do not rub, working from the inner corner outwards. Keep it off the lash line and out of your eyes.
  5. Follow with your moisturiser on the rest of the face, and SPF in the morning.

If you use a serum, apply it before the eye cream; Deyga 2% Hyaluronic Acid Serum (£22.99) is a light option. For moisturiser, see moisturiser for your skin type. For more on serums, read our face serum guide.

Morning and night

In the morning, choose a light cream or gel that sits well under make-up, and finish with sunscreen: the skin around the eyes is often forgotten. Vilvah Skin Finish Sunscreen SPF 50 PA+++ (£17.99) is a light everyday option; keep it just outside the eye area if it stings. At night you can use a richer cream or balm. The Vilvah Face Lift Kit (£35.99) pairs Vilvah's Ultra Moisturising Cream with its Under Eye Cream (Advanced), which contains bakuchiol, niacinamide, ceramides and hyaluronic acid.

Good to know

  • Patch test any new eye product on your jaw or inner arm first.
  • Keep it out of your eyes; rinse with clean water if it gets in.
  • Use clean fingers and close the jar after use.
  • Stinging, redness or swelling that does not settle is worth showing to a pharmacist or your GP.

nodes.title: Tom Ford perfume: Black Orchid, Noir Extreme, Neroli Portofino and more
nodes.body:
Tom Ford perfume covers a wide range, from dark, velvety evening scents to bright citrus colognes. Here are the Tom Ford fragrances we stock, what is in each one, when to wear it, and a few other scents in a similar mood if you want to compare.

Signature and Private Blend

Tom Ford's perfumes fall into two main lines. The Signature collection includes Black Orchid and Noir Extreme. The Private Blend collection includes Oud Wood, Neroli Portofino and Ébène Fumé, and is usually sold in smaller bottles at a higher price. Both are made for anyone to wear: "for men" on a label is only a guide.

Tom Ford Black Orchid

Tom Ford Black Orchid Parfum (£153.99, 100ml) is dark and rich. It opens on truffle and plum, moves into rum, ylang-ylang and black orchid, and settles on patchouli. It is an amber floral, made unisex, and best for evenings, special occasions and the colder months. The parfum is a stronger concentration than eau de parfum, so one or two sprays are plenty.

Tom Ford Noir Extreme

Tom Ford Noir Extreme Parfum (£144.99, 100ml) is warm and spicy-sweet. Cardamom, nutmeg, saffron, mandarin and neroli open it; rose, jasmine, orange blossom and kulfi, a milky, dessert-like accord, form the heart; vanilla, amber, sandalwood and woods make the base. It is made for men and suits evenings and cooler weather.

Tom Ford Neroli Portofino

Tom Ford Neroli Portofino Eau de Parfum (£164.99, 50ml) is the bright one. Italian bergamot, mandarin and Sicilian lemon lead into Tunisian neroli, orange flower and lavender, over a light base of amber and rosemary. It is unisex and easy to wear in the daytime, at work and on holiday.

Ébène Fumé and Oud Wood

Tom Ford Ébène Fumé (£184.99, 50ml) is smoky and woody: palo santo and black pepper, then rose and leather, over ebony wood and resin. Tom Ford Oud Wood (from £115.99, 30ml or 50ml) is smoother: oud wood, rosewood and cardamom over sandalwood, vetiver, tonka bean and amber. For more on oud, read our oud perfume guide.

Which Tom Ford perfume suits you?

  • Fresh and easy for daytime: Neroli Portofino.
  • Warm, spicy and sweet: Noir Extreme.
  • Dark, rich and dramatic: Black Orchid.
  • Smoky and woody: Ébène Fumé, or the softer Oud Wood.

The season helps too. Neroli Portofino suits spring and summer, while Black Orchid, Noir Extreme, Ébène Fumé and Oud Wood come into their own in autumn and winter. Many people keep one fresh and one warm scent and switch as the weather changes.

Other scents in a similar mood

These are different perfumes, not copies, but they share some of the same notes:

  • If you like Neroli Portofino's citrus: Acqua di Parma Colonia Pura (£32.99, 20ml), with bergamot, orange and petitgrain over jasmine, coriander, musk and cedarwood.
  • If you like Noir Extreme's spice and vanilla: Joop! Homme Le Parfum (£32.99, 75ml), with lavender and cinnamon, orange blossom and tonka bean, then vanilla, amber and woods.
  • If you like Black Orchid's rum and depth: Bvlgari Man in Black (£64.99, 100ml), with rum, spices and tobacco, leather, tuberose and iris, over guaiac wood, benzoin and tonka bean.

How to wear it

  1. Start with one or two sprays on the neck or wrists; parfums and eau de parfums are concentrated.
  2. Spray on moisturised skin so the scent has something to sit on: see our guide to layering perfume with body butter.
  3. Let it settle before you judge it. The base notes come through after the first half hour.

Good to know

  • Parfum vs eau de parfum: read extrait vs eau de parfum for what the labels mean.
  • Sizes: Black Orchid and Noir Extreme come in 100ml bottles, Neroli Portofino and Ébène Fumé in 50ml, and Oud Wood in 30ml or 50ml.
  • Gifting? Tom Ford makes a generous present; see our Christmas gift guide.
  • Store bottles away from heat and sunlight, with the cap on.
