nodes.title: Face serum guide: vitamin C, hyaluronic acid, niacinamide and how to layer them
nodes.body:
A face serum is a light, concentrated step that sits between cleansing and moisturising. Most are watery or gel-like and carry one or two key ingredients, such as vitamin C, hyaluronic acid or niacinamide. Here is what each of those ingredients is, how to choose a serum, and how to layer it.

Serum, moisturiser or face oil?

  • Water-based serums are thin and quick to absorb. They go on first, after cleansing and toning.
  • Moisturisers are creams or lotions that hold moisture in. They go on after your serum.
  • Oil serums are blends of plant oils. They can be used last at night, or mixed with a drop of moisturiser.

Vitamin C serum

Vitamin C is an antioxidant, and one of the most searched serum ingredients. Pure vitamin C (ascorbic acid) can be unstable, so many serums use a gentler, more stable form. Deyga 10% Vitamin C Face Serum (from £16.99, 20ml) uses ascorbyl glucoside, a stable form of vitamin C, with orange and citrus extracts. Use a vitamin C serum in the morning, and always finish with sunscreen. See every vitamin C serum.

Hyaluronic acid serum

Hyaluronic acid is a moisture-loving ingredient that holds water in the skin, so it suits every skin type, including oily skin. Deyga 2% Hyaluronic Acid Serum (£22.99, 20ml) combines sodium hyaluronate with glycerine, panthenol, aloe vera and centella asiatica, and is made without fragrance. Vilvah Milk Drops Hydrating Serum (from £21.99) pairs aloe vera juice and hyaluronic acid with rice milk extract and alpha arbutin. Apply either to slightly damp skin. Our Vilvah Milk Drops guide covers its full ingredient list and which size to buy.

Niacinamide, bakuchiol and ceramides

Niacinamide is a form of vitamin B3 that is easy to pair with other ingredients. If you are looking for a niacinamide serum, read the full ingredient list: niacinamide often works alongside other ingredients rather than on its own. Bakuchiol is a plant extract often used as a gentle alternative to retinol, and ceramides are lipids that are naturally found in skin. Vilvah Better Ageing Serum (£28.99, 20ml) brings all three together, with hyaluronic acid, olive squalane, blue pea flower extract and a plant peptide extract. The Vilvah AM PM Serum Kit (£47.99) pairs it with Milk Drops: Milk Drops in the morning, Better Ageing at night. For dry, mature skin, Highborn London MOISTUREBURST Serum (from £57) is a ceramide serum made to layer under moisturiser. Our peptide and bakuchiol serum guide explains these ingredients in more detail.

Face oil serums

Oil serums suit dry skin and evening routines. Deyga Rose Glow Serum (£17.99, 30ml) blends rose and saffron with coconut, pomegranate seed, rosehip, almond and jojoba oils. Deyga Beautifying Serum (from £17.99, 30ml) uses moringa, kukui, grapeseed and vetiver oils. Warm two or three drops between your palms and press them into the skin.

How to choose a face serum

  • Dry or tight skin: hyaluronic acid, ceramides or a face oil at night.
  • Oily skin: a light hyaluronic acid serum, which can be enough on its own on warm days.
  • Dull-looking skin: a vitamin C serum in the morning, with sunscreen.
  • Sensitive skin: a short, fragrance-free list, and one new product at a time.

How to layer a serum

  1. Cleanse with a face wash that suits you: see face wash for your skin type.
  2. Apply 2 or 3 drops of a water-based serum to slightly damp skin and press it in. A toner after cleansing leaves skin slightly damp: see our toner guide.
  3. Go thinnest to thickest: serum, then eye cream, then moisturiser. Read moisturiser for your skin type and our under eye cream guide.
  4. In the morning, finish with SPF. Browse every sunscreen.

You do not need several serums. One in the morning and one at night is plenty for most people.

Good to know

  • Patch test a new serum on your jaw or inner arm for 24 hours.
  • Introduce one new serum at a time, so you know what suits your skin.
  • Store serums with the cap closed, away from heat and sunlight, and use them within the time shown on the pack.
  • Stinging, redness or itching that lasts is worth showing to a pharmacist or your GP.

nodes.title: How to Check Fragrance Authenticity When Shopping Online in the UK
nodes.body:
Buying a designer fragrance online should feel considered, not confusing. If you are wondering whether a perfume is authentic, start with the seller and the details of the offer, then look at the product as a whole. No single at-home check should be treated as a certificate of authenticity.

This guide offers general shopping advice for UK buyers. It does not certify an individual bottle or describe Swansura’s supplier relationships or stock-checking procedures.

Start with the seller, not the bottle

Before ordering, check who you are actually buying from. On a marketplace, the seller may be different from the website hosting the listing. Look for clear business and contact details, delivery information and a returns policy you can read before paying.

Read recent reviews across a range of ratings and, where possible, more than one source. Look for specific accounts of purchases and how questions or problems were handled. A high star rating or a single negative comment is not enough to settle authenticity.

If a retailer claims to be an authorised stockist, look for confirmation through the brand’s own channels. Words such as “original”, “genuine” or “authentic” in a listing are claims to assess, not independent evidence.

Compare the exact fragrance and price

Compare the same fragrance name, bottle size, concentration and format. An eau de toilette, eau de parfum and gift set are not interchangeable comparisons. Check whether the listing describes a tester, refill, unboxed item or other difference in presentation.

An unusually low price is a reason to ask questions, not a verdict that a fragrance is fake. Equally, a full retail price does not establish authenticity. Consider price alongside the seller’s information and the product description rather than looking for a universal “safe” discount.

Inspect packaging, bottle and atomiser together

When your order arrives, compare it with the listing and the brand’s information for the exact version. Check the fragrance name, concentration, volume, printed wording and overall finish. Photograph anything that seems inconsistent, including misspellings, unclear printing, leaks or damage.

A different-looking box or cap is a prompt to investigate, not a conclusion. Ask the seller or brand whether the presentation is appropriate for that version rather than relying on a photograph of a different size or edition.

Look at the atomiser and bottle condition without dismantling them. A leaking or poorly functioning spray is worth raising with the seller, but spray pattern, cap weight or tube length alone should not be used to authenticate a bottle. Do not repeatedly spray a product you are concerned about merely to test it.

Understand what batch codes can tell you

A batch code identifies a production batch. It is not the same thing as the retail barcode. If you can find codes on the bottle and box, record them and ask the seller about anything unclear or inconsistent.

Third-party batch-code calculators are intended to interpret production information, not authenticate the liquid in a bottle. A returned date is not a certificate of authenticity; an unrecognised code is not, by itself, proof of a counterfeit. Calculator providers acknowledge that their information can be incomplete or incorrect. For a more reliable explanation of a code, contact the brand directly.

Do not rely on scent or longevity alone

If something smells different from what you remember, first confirm that you ordered the same fragrance and concentration. Fragrance can behave differently on different people’s skin, and storage conditions can affect its condition. A remembered scent, one spray or a shorter-than-expected wear time is not a reliable authentication test on its own.

If you have concerns about the product’s identity or condition, pause use and ask for help rather than trying internet “tests”. Do not apply a suspect fragrance to your skin to prove whether it is genuine.

Your quick fragrance authenticity checklist

  • Identify the actual seller and check contact, delivery and returns information.
  • Read recent, detailed reviews across different ratings and sources.
  • Compare the exact fragrance, concentration, size and format before judging the price.
  • Keep the order confirmation and photograph the product, packaging and any concerns.
  • Treat batch codes, packaging and atomiser details as clues, not standalone proof.
  • If something does not add up, pause use and contact the seller or brand.

What to do if you are unsure

Keep your receipt, order confirmation, box and bottle. Contact the seller through its published support channel with your order details, clear photographs and a specific explanation of the concern. Ask for an explanation and the next steps rather than assuming the cause.

You can also ask the fragrance brand whether it can help interpret the packaging or batch information. If the issue remains unresolved, seek current UK consumer guidance from Citizens Advice. This guide does not set out legal entitlements or promise a particular refund outcome.

The most useful approach is a combination of checks: understand who you are buying from, compare the precise product and ask clear questions when something needs explaining.

Further reading

  • Which?: comparing perfume prices and shopping safely
  • CheckCosmetic: batch-code information and calculator limitations

nodes.title: Goat milk soap: what it is, how to use it, and which bar to choose
nodes.body:
Goat milk soap is a bar soap made with goat milk in its recipe. It gives a creamy lather and leaves skin feeling soft rather than tight, which is why many people keep a bar by the bath or basin. This guide explains how goat milk soap is made, how to use it on your face and body, and how to choose between the goat milk soaps from Vilvah, one of the two Indian natural brands Swansura is an official UK partner of.

What is goat milk soap?

Every true bar soap is made by mixing oils or butters with lye (sodium hydroxide). The two react together to form soap, a process called saponification. In goat milk soap, fresh goat milk goes into the recipe, which gives the bar a creamy lather. You will see sodium hydroxide at the end of the ingredient lists below: that is how all bar soap is made.

Vilvah makes its goat milk bars by hand with farm-fresh goat milk and a base of plant oils such as extra virgin olive, coconut and castor oil. Coconut oil gives the bubbly lather, olive oil a gentle feel and castor oil a cushioned foam. For the rest of the brand, see our Vilvah guide.

The Vilvah goat milk soaps

  • Classic Goat Milk Soap (£9.99, 115g): goat milk, olive, coconut and castor oils, lightly scented with lavender essential oil. Six ingredients in all, and listed as suiting dry and sensitive skin.
  • Classic Rose Goat Milk Soap (£9.99, 125g): goat milk with rose petals, rose hydrosol, French pink clay, shea butter and rice bran oil, scented with rose and geranium essential oils.
  • Charcoal Goat Milk Soap (£9.99, 115g): activated charcoal with goat milk, for a clean-feeling daily wash. The charcoal gives the bar its colour.

All three are in our goat milk soap collection. One bar that looks similar is not a goat milk soap: Vilvah’s Cucumber, Curd & Mint Soap (£9.99) is made with cucumber juice, curd and mint leaves, for a cool, zesty morning wash.

Which bar should you choose?

  • A soft, simple scent: the Classic bar, with lavender.
  • A floral scent: Classic Rose.
  • A clean-feeling wash: Charcoal.
  • Something fresh and minty: Cucumber, Curd & Mint.
  • A bar without milk: Deyga’s Shea Saffron Bath Bar (£15.99) and Rose Pink Clay Bath Bar (£14.99) are made with raw shea butter and coconut and olive oils. Our body wash and bath bar guide compares them with Deyga’s other bars and body washes.

How to use goat milk soap

  1. Wet your skin and the bar, then work up a lather between your hands.
  2. Massage the foam over damp face or body, keeping it away from your eyes.
  3. Rinse well with warm water and pat dry.
  4. Follow with a moisturiser or body lotion if your skin tends to feel dry.
  5. Keep the bar on a draining soap dish between uses. A handmade bar left sitting in water softens quickly.

The Classic, Classic Rose and Cucumber bars contain essential oils, so patch test before first use.

Goat milk shampoo and hair care

Goat milk is not only for soap. Vilvah Goat Milk Shampoo (£15.99, 250ml) is a creamy shampoo with goat milk, jasmine flower water and hydrolysed pea protein, with a light jasmine and citrus scent. Vilvah Goat Milk Hair Mask (£31.99) pairs goat milk with ceramides and argan oil to condition dry, frizzy lengths. Buy them together in the Goat Milk Hair Kit (£34.99), or try the shampoo with Vilvah’s Cream Conditioner in the Bestseller Hair Kit (£27.99). Our natural shampoo guide covers how to choose a shampoo for dry hair.

Goat milk for the body

The Vilvah Milk Body Kit (£44.99) pairs a Goat Milk Body Wash, made with goat milk, chamomile water and coconut oil and scented with vanilla, with a Milk Body Lotion. If you were looking for a goat milk body lotion, note that the Milk Body Lotion (£25.99) is made with oat milk, ceramide NP and olive squalane: the goat milk in this kit is in the body wash. For richer body care after a soap, read our body butter guide.

Good to know

  • Goat milk soap is not vegan, because it contains goat milk.
  • Every skin is different. If you have a skin condition, ask a pharmacist or GP before trying a new soap.
  • A goat milk bar wrapped in tissue makes an easy gift: see our stocking fillers and stocking fillers guide.

nodes.title: Indian skincare in the UK: the key ingredients, Vilvah and Deyga, and how to start
nodes.body:
Indian skincare grows out of ingredients found in Indian kitchens and gardens: turmeric, neem, saffron, rose water, amla and coconut oil. Many people in the UK grew up with them through family routines, and many more are discovering them now. This guide explains the key ingredients, shows which products from Vilvah and Deyga actually contain them (checked against each full ingredient list), and covers how to buy Indian skincare in the UK without waiting for a parcel from India.

What makes Indian skincare different?

Two things stand out. First, the ingredients: many come from Ayurveda, India’s traditional system of wellbeing, and from everyday cooking, so the labels read like a spice rack. Deyga even lists many ingredients with their Sanskrit names, such as Haridra for turmeric, Nimba for neem, Kumkuma for saffron and Satapatrika for rose. Second, the formats: powder face packs you mix with water, oils massaged into the scalp before washing, and handmade bars. These are cosmetic products, not Ayurvedic medicines, and we describe them that way.

The key ingredients, and where to find them

Turmeric (haldi)

Turmeric is part of the Indian haldi ceremony before a wedding, when a turmeric paste is spread on the bride and groom. You will find it in the Deyga Neem & Turmeric Bath Bar (£14.99), made with coconut oil, neem hydrosol, turmeric and shea butter, and in the Deyga Orange & Almond Face Pack (£19.99), a three-ingredient powder of sun-dried orange pulp and zest, almond meal and turmeric. Turmeric can colour towels and nails, so rinse well.

Neem

Neem is a tree grown across India, and its leaves and seeds are used in hair and skin care. Deyga Neem Seed Oil (£14.99) has one ingredient: neem seed oil, with a strong, earthy scent. The Deyga Spirulina Matcha Face Pack (£17.99) mixes neem leaf with spirulina, matcha, moringa and aloe vera powder.

Saffron (kesar or kumkuma)

Saffron is one of the most prized spices in Indian cooking and a long-standing beauty ingredient. The Deyga Rose Glow Serum (£17.99) is a face oil of native rose and saffron in virgin coconut, pomegranate seed, rosehip, almond and jojoba oils. The Deyga Shea Saffron Bath Bar (£15.99) pairs saffron with raw shea butter, and the Vilvah Milk Mud Mask (£19.99) combines kaolin clay, licorice root, oat milk and saffron extract.

Rose water (gulab jal)

Rose water is a staple of Indian dressing tables, used to refresh the face or mix face packs. Deyga Pure Rose Water Toner (£11.99) has two ingredients: rose and distilled water. It is also the classic liquid for mixing a powder face pack.

Clay and multani mitti

Multani mitti, or fuller’s earth, is the traditional Indian clay for face packs. Our clay products use kaolin and French pink clay instead, such as the Milk Mud Mask above. Our face mask guide explains how to use clay masks and powder packs.

Amla, bhringraj and hibiscus for hair

Oiling the hair before washing is one of the best-known Indian routines. Deyga’s Hair Growth Oil (£14.99) is a coconut, almond and castor oil base with amla, bhringraj, hibiscus, fenugreek, curry leaves and vetiver: a classic Indian herbal hair oil. Vilvah Anti-Frizz Hair Serum (£28.99) is a lighter, leave-in option with black seed oil, curry leaf oil, hibiscus oil and amla extract, and Vilvah Herbal Shampoo (£15.99, 250ml) includes neem leaf, amla and basil leaf water. Read our hair oil guide for how to oil your hair.

Beetroot and goat milk

Two newer favourites: the Deyga Beetroot Lip Balm (from £10.99) is made with beetroot extract, almond, avocado and jojoba oils and shea butter, and Vilvah builds much of its range on goat milk (see our goat milk soap guide).

A simple way to start

  1. Cleanse: a handmade bar such as the Neem & Turmeric bar for the body, or a gentle face wash.
  2. Refresh: pat on rose water with clean hands or a cotton pad.
  3. Nourish: a few drops of a face oil such as the Rose Glow Serum in the evening.
  4. Once a week: a powder face pack mixed with rose water, or a clay mask.
  5. Hair: oil the scalp and lengths an hour or more before washing, then shampoo.

Many of these products contain essential oils or strongly scented plant ingredients, so patch test anything you leave on the skin, and keep powders and oils away from the eyes. For which brand suits your skin type, read Deyga or Vilvah; for adding a serum, see our face serum guide.

Buying Indian skincare in the UK

  • Official UK partner: Swansura is an official UK partner of both Deyga and Vilvah, so every product is genuine. Read more in our brand guides: Deyga Organics in the UK and Vilvah in the UK.
  • Shipped from the UK: orders leave our UK stock, so there is no wait for a parcel from India and no import charge at your door.
  • Full ingredient lists: almost every product page has the full ingredient list on its Ingredients tab, so you can check before you buy.
  • Delivery: UK delivery is free on orders over £40, and unopened items can be returned within 14 days.

Browse all our natural skincare, or shop by brand: Vilvah and Deyga.

nodes.title: Toner for dry skin: how to choose one, and which suits oily or sensitive skin
nodes.body:
A face toner is the light, watery step between cleansing and moisturising. Old-fashioned toners were often astringent and full of alcohol, which is why many people with dry skin still avoid them. Today most toners are gentle and hydrating instead. Here is how to choose a toner for dry skin, which toner suits oily or sensitive skin, and how to use one.

What does a toner do?

After cleansing, a toner takes off any last traces of cleanser or tap water and gives skin a first layer of moisture. Skin that is slightly damp takes serum and moisturiser more evenly, so a toner makes the rest of your routine easier to apply. It is an optional step: if your skin feels comfortable without one, you can skip it.

How to choose a toner for dry skin

  • Look for hydrating ingredients such as glycerine, rose water or aloe near the top of the list.
  • Avoid a high level of alcohol (listed as alcohol denat. or SD alcohol), which can leave dry skin feeling tight.
  • Keep it short if your skin is sensitive too: fewer ingredients make it easier to see what suits you.
  • Go easy on acids such as glycolic acid, which gently exfoliate. Dry skin may prefer them two or three times a week rather than daily.

Hydrating toners for dry and sensitive skin

Deyga Pure Rose Water Toner (£11.99, 100ml) is the simplest toner we stock: just rose (Rosa centifolia) and distilled water, with no alcohol. It is a classic rose water toner that you can spritz on or sweep over with a cotton pad, and it also works as a midday refresher over bare skin. It is a good first toner for dry or sensitive skin.

Highborn London Diamond Toner (£25, 100ml) is a moisturising toner made to follow Highborn London Crystal Cleanser (£24) as the second step of the Highborn routine. Press it in with your hands or sweep it on with a cotton pad before serum and moisturiser.

A toner with a gentle acid

Vilvah Milk Face Toner (£19.99, 100ml) is water and earth marine water with glycerin, a xylitol-based moisturising blend and rice milk extract, plus glycolic acid, a gentle exfoliating acid. That makes it a good fit for normal and combination skin that wants a smoother feel. If your skin is dry or sensitive, start with two or three evenings a week, and wear sunscreen during the day while you use it.

Toner for oily skin

Oily skin still benefits from a light, hydrating toner: stripping skin with alcohol can leave it feeling tight while it still looks shiny. Deyga Tea Tree Facial Toner (£14.99, 100ml) is three ingredients: tea tree, mulethi (liquorice root) and distilled water, and Deyga makes it without alcohol. Its fresh, herbal feel suits oily and combination skin. Tea tree is an essential oil, so patch test it first if your skin is sensitive. More ideas for oily skin.

Which toner suits you?

  • Dry skin: Deyga Pure Rose Water Toner or Highborn London Diamond Toner, every day.
  • Sensitive skin: the two-ingredient rose water toner, and a patch test first.
  • Normal or combination skin: Vilvah Milk Face Toner, a few times a week to start.
  • Oily skin: Deyga Tea Tree Facial Toner.

How to use a toner

  1. Cleanse with a gentle face wash such as Deyga Oat Milk Face Wash (£12.99), then pat your face almost dry. Our guide to face wash for your skin type helps you choose.
  2. Apply the toner with clean hands or a cotton pad, pressing it over the face and neck. Avoid the eyes.
  3. While skin is still damp, apply a serum such as Deyga 2% Hyaluronic Acid Serum (£22.99). Read our face serum guide.
  4. Finish with moisturiser. Dry skin likes something richer, such as Deyga Deep Moisturising Face Cream (£18.99); see moisturiser for your skin type.
  5. In the morning, add sunscreen as the last step.

Good to know

  • Toner is not a cleanser: it will not take off make-up or sunscreen on its own.
  • Rose water also mixes face packs: see our face mask guide.
  • Patch test any new toner on your jaw or inner arm for 24 hours.
  • Stinging, redness or flaking that lasts is worth showing to a pharmacist or your GP.

A mini perfume set is a box of small bottles, usually 4ml to 15ml each, from one perfume house. It lets someone try several scents before buying a full bottle, keep a favourite in their bag, or simply enjoy a little collection. Here is what is inside the miniature sets we stock, starting with Jimmy Choo and Dior.

Why choose a mini perfume set?

  • To try before buying: wear each scent for a day or two and see which one you reach for.
  • For travel and handbags: small bottles take up little room.

nodes.title: Frizzy hair: serum, oil or mask? How to choose for dry, frizzy hair
nodes.body:
Frizz is one of the most common hair complaints, and it is usually a sign that hair is dry. The good news is that the fix is mostly moisture and a gentle routine, not a cupboard full of products. Here is what causes frizz, when to reach for a hair serum for frizzy hair, a pre-wash oil or a hair mask for dry hair, and how to put them together.

Why hair goes frizzy

Each strand has a smooth outer layer. When hair is dry, that layer lifts a little, strands lose their shine and they take in moisture from damp air, so they swell and stop lying flat. Rough towel drying, hot water, heat styling and brushing hair while it is wet all make it worse. That is why frizz often gets worse in winter, when indoor heating dries hair out, and on wet British days.

Serum, oil or mask: what each one does

  • A hair serum is a light leave-in for the lengths and ends. It smooths the surface of dry hair after washing, so flyaways lie flatter and hair looks glossier.
  • A hair oil is usually richer and used before washing, on the scalp and lengths, then shampooed out.
  • A hair mask is a thicker conditioner you leave on for longer, once or twice a week, for hair that feels rough and dry.

Most dry, frizzy hair does well with all three in their place: a mask weekly, a conditioner every wash and a few drops of serum to finish.

Hair serum for frizzy hair

Vilvah Anti-Frizz Hair Serum (£28.99, 30ml) is a light oil serum made without silicones. Its ingredient list is short: black seed oil, aloe vera, curry leaf oil, jasmine flower extract, hibiscus oil, glycerine, arnica oil, fenugreek seed extract, baobab oil, amla fruit extract, vitamin E and cypress essential oil.

Warm two or three drops between your palms and smooth them over the mid-lengths and ends of towel-dried or dry hair, keeping away from the roots. Start with less: you can always add a drop, but too much leaves hair looking greasy. It also comes as the Vilvah Shampoo & Hair Serum Kit (£25.99) with the Goat Milk Shampoo. Browse every hair serum for frizzy hair.

Hair mask for dry hair

Vilvah Goat Milk Hair Mask (£31.99, 200g) is made with goat milk, ceramides, argan oil, vitamin E, glycerine and a seaweed-based moisturising blend. Vilvah says it can be used as a mask, as a conditioner or as a small leave-in amount for styling.

As a mask, smooth it through clean, damp hair from the mid-lengths to the ends, comb it through with a wide-tooth comb, leave it for 10 to 15 minutes and rinse. Once or twice a week is plenty. The Vilvah Goat Milk Hair Kit (£34.99) pairs the mask with the Goat Milk Shampoo. See more hair masks for dry hair.

Shampoo and conditioner for dry, frizzy hair

A creamy shampoo and a rich conditioner do most of the daily work. Vilvah Goat Milk Shampoo (£12.99) is made with goat milk, jasmine flower water, jojoba oil, panthenol and hydrolysed pea protein. Follow it with Vilvah Cream Conditioner (£12.99), made without silicones and with tucuma butter, broccoli seed oil, aloe vera and pea protein; Vilvah says you can also leave it on for up to 15 minutes as a mask.

If you prefer something lighter, Deyga Rice Water Shampoo (from £10.99) uses rice water and mild coconut-derived cleansers, and Deyga Soy Milk Conditioner (from £11.99) adds soybean extract, argan oil and provitamin B5 without weighing hair down. For more on choosing one, read our natural shampoo guide.

Pre-wash hair oil for dry hair

Oiling before you wash is a long-standing Indian hair ritual, and it suits dry lengths well. Deyga Hair Growth Oil (£14.99, 100ml) blends virgin coconut, almond, castor and sunflower oils infused with amla, hibiscus, fenugreek and bhringraj, with an applicator tip for the scalp. Leave it on for an hour or overnight, then shampoo it out. Our hair oil guide explains amla, bhringraj and castor oil and how to oil step by step, and you can browse every hair oil for dry hair.

A simple routine for frizzy hair

  1. Once a week, before washing: massage a little oil into the scalp and lengths and leave it on for an hour.
  2. Wash with lukewarm water, not hot, and a creamy shampoo. Lather mainly at the scalp.
  3. Condition every time, from the mid-lengths to the ends. Once or twice a week, swap the conditioner for a hair mask.
  4. Blot, do not rub. Squeeze water out with a soft towel or an old cotton T-shirt.
  5. Detangle gently with a wide-tooth comb, starting at the ends. A wooden comb such as the Vilvah Neem Wood Comb (£9.99) glides through without tugging.
  6. Finish with two or three drops of serum on the ends, then air dry or blow-dry on a cool setting.

Want it all in one box? The Vilvah Frizz Free Hair Kit (£35.99) holds the Goat Milk Shampoo, Cream Conditioner and Anti-Frizz Hair Serum.

Good to know

  • Less is more with serum and oil: start with a few drops and add more only if your ends still feel dry.
  • Patch test products with essential oils, such as the serum and the pre-wash oil, before first use.
  • Silk or satin pillowcases and a loose plait at night can help hair stay smoother by morning.
  • Sudden changes in your hair or scalp, such as itching, soreness or hair loss, are worth showing to a pharmacist or your GP.

nodes.title: Al Haramain Amber Oud: every edition compared, from Gold to Tobacco
nodes.body:
Al Haramain's Amber Oud is a family of eau de parfums rather than a single scent. Each edition has its own colour and its own character, from the sweet, fruity Gold to the spiced Tobacco and the fresh, herbal Carbon. Here is every Al Haramain Amber Oud edition we stock, side by side, with its notes, sizes and the kind of person it suits.

Is there oud in Amber Oud?

Amber Oud is the name of the line. The note lists we hold for these editions do not name oud: they are built on amber, woods, musk, vanilla and resins, with fruit, flowers, spice or herbs on top depending on the edition. If you want a perfume that puts oud at the centre, read our oud perfume guide. If you want a warm, amber-led scent with an Arabian feel, read on.

Sweet and fruity: the original and the Gold Edition

Al Haramain Amber Oud Gold Edition (from £32.99, 60ml, 100ml or 200ml) opens with bergamot and green notes, moves into melon, pineapple, amber and sweet notes, and dries down to vanilla, musk and woods. It is the edition to choose if you like sweet, golden, fruity scents.

The original Al Haramain Amber Oud (£38.99, 60ml) carries the same note list in our listings: bergamot and green notes, then amber, melon, pineapple and sweet notes, then vanilla, musk and woods. The brand sells them as separate editions, so expect them to be close relatives.

For a stronger version, Amber Oud Extreme Gold Edition (from £36.99, 60ml or 100ml) is an extrait de parfum with the same listed notes. An extrait has a higher concentration of fragrance oils than an eau de parfum; our guide to extrait vs eau de parfum explains the labels.

Warm and spiced: Ruby, Tobacco and Black

  • Amber Oud Ruby Edition (from £41.99, 100ml, 120ml or 200ml): saffron and bitter almond, then jasmine and cedarwood, over ambergris, woods and musk. Spiced, nutty and floral, a smooth choice for evenings.
  • Amber Oud Tobacco Edition (£32.99, 60ml): tobacco leaf, cinnamon, black pepper and ginger, then vanilla, clove, star anise, cacao and tonka bean, over tobacco, dried fruits and woods. The richest and sweetest of the spiced editions, made for winter nights.
  • Amber Oud Black Edition (£39.99, 100ml): cardamom, grapefruit and lavender, then leather, amber and orange blossom, over benzoin, ambergris and vetiver. Darker and drier, with a leather heart.

Fresh and woody: Bleu and Carbon

  • Amber Oud Bleu Edition (from £38.99, 60ml, 100ml or 200ml): grapefruit, lemon, mint and pink pepper, then ginger, nutmeg and jasmine, over incense, vetiver, cedar, sandalwood, patchouli, labdanum and white musk. Crisp at the start and woody underneath, easy to wear all year.
  • Amber Oud Carbon Edition (from £35.99, 60ml, 100ml or 200ml): lavender, rosemary and bergamot, then sage, cedarwood and geranium, over vetiver, musk, amber and moss. A clean, herbal scent sold as a men's fragrance, good for the office.

Floral: the White Edition

Amber Oud White Edition (from £34.99, 60ml, 100ml or 200ml) is sold as a women's fragrance: bergamot and orange, then jasmine, rose and freesia, over musk, vanilla and patchouli. It is the lightest and most floral of the family, an easy pick for daytime.

Which Amber Oud edition should you choose?

  • You like sweet, fruity scents: Gold Edition, or Extreme Gold for a richer version.
  • You want something warm for winter: Tobacco Edition or Ruby Edition.
  • You like leather and dry woods: Black Edition.
  • You want a fresh everyday scent: Bleu Edition, or Carbon for a herbal, barbershop style.
  • You prefer florals: White Edition.

Most editions are unisex; Carbon is sold for men and White for women, but wear whichever you like. Prefer amber without the fruit? The sister scent Al Haramain Amber Musk (£39.99, 100ml) is amber and floral notes over musk, woods, vanilla and resins.

How to wear it

These are full, warm eau de parfums, so start with a spray or two on the neck and wrists rather than a cloud. They sit well on moisturised skin; our guide to layering oud with body butter shows how. For the wider family of Arabian scents, see our Arabian perfume guide.

Good to know

  • Sizes vary by edition: Gold, Bleu, Carbon and White come in 60ml, 100ml and 200ml; check each listing for the size you want.
  • As a gift: the warmer editions make a generous Christmas present. See our perfume gift sets guide for more ideas.
  • Every bottle is 100% authentic and dispatched from the UK, with free UK delivery over £40.

nodes.title: Paco Rabanne perfume: 1 Million, Invictus, Phantom, Fame and Lady Million compared
nodes.body:
Paco Rabanne's fragrance names can be confusing: 1 Million, Invictus and Phantom for men, Fame, Lady Million and Olympéa for women, each in several versions. Here is every Paco Rabanne perfume line we stock, with its notes, the versions on offer and who each one suits.

Paco Rabanne for him

1 Million: warm and spicy

Paco Rabanne 1 Million Eau de Toilette (£78.99, 200ml) opens with blood mandarin, grapefruit and mint, moves to cinnamon, rose and spice, and settles on amber, leather, woody notes and Indian patchouli. It is sweet, spiced and confident, a natural choice for nights out and colder weather. The 1 Million Elixir, which you will find in the men's miniature set (£50.99, 4 x 5ml), takes a different route: apple and davana, then Damask rose, osmanthus and cedar, over vanilla absolute, tonka bean and patchouli.

Invictus: fresh and marine

Paco Rabanne Invictus Eau de Toilette (£78.99, 200ml) is the fresh one: sea notes, grapefruit and mandarin orange, then bay leaf and jasmine, over ambergris, guaiac wood, oakmoss and patchouli. It suits everyday wear, the office and warmer days. For a present, the Invictus Eau de Toilette Gift Set (£78.99) adds a 10ml spray to the 200ml bottle, and the Invictus Eau de Toilette & Deodorant Gift Set (£64.99) pairs a 100ml bottle with a deodorant spray and a 10ml spray.

Invictus Victory Eau de Parfum Extrême (£65.99, 100ml) is the warmer sister: pink pepper and lemon, then olibanum and lavender, over vanilla, tonka bean and amber. Choose it for evenings and winter; choose the original Invictus for daytime and summer.

Phantom: aromatic lavender

Phantom is built around lavender. The eau de toilette, found in both men's miniature sets, opens with lavender, lemon zest and Amalfi lemon, adds apple and a smoky, earthy heart, and dries down to vanilla, lavender and vetiver. The Phantom Parfum Spray (£20.99, 15ml) is richer: cardamom, bergamot, lemon and rhubarb, then lavender, geranium, patchouli and cedar, over vanilla, tolu balsam and vetiver. Its small size is a good way to try the parfum before a bigger bottle.

XS Black: woody and herbal

Paco Rabanne XS Black Eau de Toilette (£44.99, 100ml) mixes mint, bergamot and lemon with juniper berries, coriander and geranium, over oakmoss, sandalwood and rosemary. It is the most herbal and woody of the men's range.

Paco Rabanne for her

Fame: mango, jasmine and incense

The Fame Eau de Parfum (£78.99, 80ml refillable) opens on mango and bergamot, moves to jasmine and olibanum, and ends on vanilla and sandalwood: fruity at first, then smooth and softly resinous. It also comes as the Fame Eau de Parfum Gift Set (£56.99, 50ml + 10ml).

  • Fame Parfum (10ml, £19.99) adds pink pepper, patchouli and frankincense, over benzoin, sandalwood and musk: deeper and more resinous.
  • Fame Eau de Parfum Intense (30ml, £46.99) swaps the mango for coconut water, pink pepper and bergamot, with jasmine, incense and ylang-ylang over sandalwood, cedarwood and musk.
  • Not sure which? The Fame Eau de Parfum & Parfum Mini Set (£32.99, 4ml + 4ml) lets you try the eau de parfum and the parfum side by side.

Lady Million: honeyed and floral

Lady Million Eau de Parfum (£29.99, 15ml) opens with raspberry, neroli and Amalfi lemon, blooms into jasmine, African orange flower and gardenia, and finishes on white honey, patchouli and amber. It is bright and golden, made for parties and celebrations. Lady Million Royal (£46.99, 30ml) is simpler, with just three notes: pomegranate, white flowers and cashmeran.

Olympéa and Ultraviolet

  • Olympéa pairs water jasmine, green mandarin and ginger flower with vanilla and a touch of salt, over ambergris, cashmere wood and sandalwood (in the women's miniature set, £50.99). Olympéa Flora Eau de Parfum Intense (£63.99, 80ml) is fruitier: black currant, sorbet and pink pepper, then rose and peony, over patchouli, cashmere wood, vanilla and salt.
  • Ultraviolet Eau de Parfum (£45.99, 80ml) is the spiciest of the women's range: pepper, pimento, coriander, apricot and almond, then violet, osmanthus, rose and jasmine, over amber, vanilla, patchouli and cedar. A warm pick for autumn and winter.

Which Paco Rabanne should you choose?

  • Sweet and spicy for him: 1 Million, or Invictus Victory for vanilla and amber.
  • Fresh and easy for him: Invictus.
  • Lavender and clean: Phantom.
  • Fruity floral for her: Fame or Olympéa Flora.
  • Honeyed and celebratory: Lady Million.
  • Warm and spicy for her: Ultraviolet.

Gift sets and miniatures

Miniature sets are the easiest way to try several scents before choosing a full bottle. The men's miniature eau de toilette set (£27.99, 3 x 4ml) holds 1 Million, Invictus and Phantom; the 4 x 5ml set adds 1 Million Elixir. For her, the women's miniature set (£50.99) holds Lady Million, Olympéa, Fame eau de parfum and Fame parfum. Our mini perfume sets guide compares minis from other houses, and the perfume gift sets guide has more ideas for Christmas.

Good to know

  • Eau de toilette, eau de parfum or parfum? The names tell you how concentrated the fragrance is; our guide to extrait vs eau de parfum explains the labels.
  • Start small: a spray or two on the neck and wrists is enough for these scents.

nodes.title: Foot cream: how to look after dry, rough feet at home
nodes.body:
Feet have thicker skin than the rest of the body and few oil glands, so they are often the first place to feel dry, especially in winter, when boots, tights and central heating all take their toll. A good foot cream, used regularly, keeps heels and soles feeling soft and comfortable. Here is how to choose one, and how to fit it into a simple at-home pedicure.

Why feet get so dry

The skin on your heels and soles takes your weight all day. It is naturally thick, and when it dries out it can feel rough and tight. Hot baths, long showers, walking barefoot on hard floors and closed shoes in heated rooms all make it drier. Moisturising little and often works better than an occasional rescue.

Foot cream or foot butter?

  • A foot cream contains water as well as oils and butters, so it sinks in quickly. It suits daily use, morning or night.
  • A foot butter or balm has no water: it is a solid blend of oils, butters and wax that sits on the skin for longer. It suits very dry heels and works well at night under cotton socks.

Foot cream: Vilvah Foot Care Cream

Vilvah Foot Care Cream (£16, 100ml) is a rich cream with four butters (shea, avocado, mango and cocoa), sunflower, argan and kalonji (black seed) oils, glycerine and a little peppermint oil for a cool, fresh scent. Massage it into clean, dry feet, ideally before bed. It also comes as the Vilvah Foot Cream & Body Lotion Kit (£37.99), paired with the Milk Body Lotion (oat milk, ceramide, olive squalane and jojoba oil) for the rest of the body.

Foot butter: Deyga Foot Butter

Deyga Foot Butter (£12.99, 40g) is a short-ingredient balm: virgin coconut oil, olive oil, refined beeswax, vitamin E and vanilla essential oil. Warm a little between your fingers and work it into heels, soles and toes. For a richer finish, put it on at night and slip on cotton socks. It contains beeswax, so it is not vegan.

Already have a favourite body butter? A rich one such as Deyga Rose & Geranium Body Butter (£15.99) works on feet too; our body butter guide explains how to use it.

A simple at-home pedicure

  1. Soak. Dissolve two spoonfuls of Deyga Foot Soak Powder (£16.99, 160g) in a bowl of warm water. It blends sea salt and Himalayan pink salt with rose, lemon and peppermint oil. Soak for 10 to 15 minutes, no longer.
  2. Scrub. Massage Deyga Foot Scrub (£17.99, 100g) over damp feet in slow circles, focusing on the heels. Granulated sugar gives it a gentle grit, in coconut and almond oils with shea butter. Rinse with warm water. Once or twice a week is enough.
  3. Dry well, especially between the toes.
  4. Moisturise with foot cream or foot butter, then put on clean cotton socks if it is bedtime.

The Deyga Mini Foot Spa Combo (£35.99) puts the soak, the scrub and the foot butter in one box, which also makes an easy Christmas present. A natural Deyga Organic Loofah (£12.99) is handy for a quick buff of the heels in the shower. For scrubs for the rest of the body, see our body scrub guide.

Everyday habits for comfortable feet

  • Moisturise daily, ideally after a bath or shower, while skin is still slightly damp.
  • Keep showers warm, not hot, and do not leave feet soaking for long. Our natural body wash guide has a simple shower routine for dry skin.
  • Wear socks around the house in winter rather than walking barefoot on cold, hard floors.
  • Do not use foot cream between the toes; keep that skin dry.

Good to know

  • Patch test before first use: the cream, butter and soak all contain essential oils, and the scrub contains almond oil.
  • Do not scrub broken or sore skin.
  • If you have diabetes or poor circulation, ask your GP or a podiatrist before soaking or scrubbing your feet.
  • Painful, deep or bleeding cracks in the heels, or any change you are unsure about, are worth showing to a pharmacist, your GP or a podiatrist.

nodes.title: Mugler perfume: Alien, Angel and Les Exceptions compared
nodes.body:
Mugler's fragrances fall into a few clear families: Alien, built around jasmine and amber; Angel, sweet and gourmand; the fresh Mugler Colognes; and the Les Exceptions collection. Here is every Mugler perfume we stock, with its notes, the sizes on offer and who each one suits.

Mugler Alien: jasmine and white amber

Mugler Alien Eau de Parfum (from £50.99, 30ml or 90ml, refillable) has just three notes: jasmine sambac, cashmeran wood and white amber. That short list makes it clear and easy to read on the skin: bright jasmine first, then a smooth, slightly powdery wood and a warm amber finish. It is a statement scent for evenings and colder weather.

Alien Goddess Supra Florale Eau de Parfum (from £26.99, 10ml, 60ml or 90ml) keeps the jasmine but makes it more floral: a cactus flower accord, jasmine grandiflorum and everlasting flower absolute. The original Alien Goddess (bergamot and coconut water, jasmine and heliotrope, over Bourbon vanilla and cashmeran) is in our Alien Goddess gift set, currently out of stock.

Alien Man

The Alien Man Eau de Toilette & Body Shampoo Travel Set (£57.99) pairs a refillable 100ml eau de toilette with a 50ml body shampoo. The scent opens with beech wood, dill, anise, lavender, lemon, mint and thyme, moves to leather, osmanthus, pepper and geranium, and dries down to white amber, cashmeran and vanilla: herbal at first, then warm and leathery.

Mugler Angel: sweet and gourmand

Mugler Angel Eau de Parfum (£44.99, 25ml) is the dessert of the family. Cotton candy, coconut, cassis and fruit open it; honey, red berries, plum and flowers fill the heart; and patchouli, chocolate, caramel, vanilla and tonka bean make the base. The contrast between the sugary notes and the earthy patchouli is what gives it its character. A bold pick for winter nights and parties.

  • Angel Elixir Eau de Parfum (from £57.99, 50ml or 100ml, refillable star bottle): pink pepper, then ylang-ylang, orange blossom, jasmine and sandalwood, over Bourbon vanilla and amber. More floral than Angel, with a warm, cosy finish.
  • Angel Nova Eau de Toilette (£50.99, 50ml): lychee and bergamot, rose and magnolia, over akigalawood and amberwood. The lightest and fruitiest of the Angel scents, easy for daytime and spring.

Mugler Les Exceptions

Les Exceptions is Mugler's collection of eau de parfums, both unisex and in 80ml bottles. You will also find them in our niche perfume edit.

  • Les Exceptions Wonder Bouquet (£60.99): shiso, lily of the valley, petitgrain, orange and tangerine, then brioche, jasmine sambac, tuberose, orange blossom and rose, over beeswax, hazelnut, vanilla and cashmeran. A rich floral with a soft, bakery-sweet edge.
  • Les Exceptions Mystic Aromatic (£60.99): thyme, basil, clary sage and fig leaf, then grey amber, over Peru balsam and cedarwood. Green and herbal, with a resinous base.

Mugler Colognes: four 10ml minis

The Mugler Colognes are fresh eau de toilettes in 10ml sprays at £14.99 each, a low-cost way to try something new:

  • Blow It Up: sorbet, vetiver and black currant.
  • Fly Away: grapefruit, a green cannabis accord and vetiver.
  • Heal Your Mind (sold for men): lavender, hazelnut and vanilla.
  • Love You All: blue liquorice, white amber and musk.

Small sizes like these make easy stocking fillers; our mini perfume sets guide has more ideas.

Which Mugler perfume should you choose?

  • You like warm, statement florals: Alien, or Alien Goddess Supra Florale for more flowers.
  • You love sweet, dessert-like scents: Angel, or Angel Elixir for a more floral version.
  • You want something light and fruity: Angel Nova.
  • Buying for him: the Alien Man set.
  • You like something different and unisex: Les Exceptions Wonder Bouquet or Mystic Aromatic.
  • You want to try before you commit: a 10ml Mugler Cologne, or the 10ml Alien Goddess Supra Florale.

Good to know

  • Refillable bottles: Alien, Angel Elixir and the Alien Man eau de toilette come in bottles made to be refilled.

nodes.title: Lip balm for dry lips: SPF, tinted or natural, and how to choose
nodes.body:
Cold wind, central heating and hot drinks all leave lips dry in winter, and a good lip balm is the simplest fix. But balms are not all the same: some carry an SPF, some add a sheer tint, and some are just a few plant oils, butters and wax. Here is how to choose a lip balm for dry lips, what is inside each type and how to get the most from it.

What a lip balm does

Lips have a very thin outer layer and no oil glands of their own, so they dry out faster than the rest of the face. A balm puts a soft layer of oils, butters and wax over them, which keeps them feeling comfortable for longer. Most balms are built from the same few things: plant oils such as almond, avocado or jojoba; butters such as shea, mango or kokum; and a wax, often beeswax, that holds it all together.

SPF lip balm

Lips burn too, on bright winter days, ski trips and holidays as much as in summer. Vilvah Milk Lip Balm SPF 30 PA+++ (£9.99) uses mineral filters, zinc oxide and titanium dioxide, in a base of coconut oil, shea butter, soy butter, kokum butter and soy milk extract, with a soft vanilla note. Apply it before going outside, and reapply often, especially after eating, drinking or swimming. It works on its own or under lipstick.

Tinted lip balm

A tinted lip balm adds a sheer wash of colour as well as moisture, so it can stand in for a lipstick on busy days.

  • Deyga Beetroot Lip Balm Classic (from £10.99, 10g pot) takes its rosy tint from beetroot extract, in almond, avocado and jojoba oils with shea butter and beeswax. The same balm comes as a twist-up Beetroot Lip Balm Stick (from £13.99, 5.5g) for your pocket. We compare the two in Deyga Beetroot Lip Balm: stick or pot.
  • Vilvah Rose Milk Lip Balm (£9.99) gives a soft pink tint, with paneer rose extract, olive squalane, avocado butter, shea butter and vitamin E.
  • Vilvah Mango Shake Lip Balm (£9.99) leaves a reddish-orange tint, with Alphonso mango pulp extract, mango butter, coconut milk and olive squalane.
  • Vilvah Filter Kaapi Lip Balm (£9.99) has a subtle brown tint inspired by South Indian filter coffee, with coffee oil, coffee extract, shea butter, coconut milk and almond oil.
  • Vilvah Grape Fruit Lip Balm (£6.99) has just six ingredients, with a little red iron oxide for a sheer tint and grapefruit essential oil for a zesty scent.

Can't choose? The Vilvah Tinted Lip Balm Kit (£17) puts two tinted balms in one box.

Natural lip balm with a short ingredient list

If you prefer a plain balm with nothing extra, look for a short list of oils, butter and wax.

  • Deyga Shea Butter Lip Balm (£9.99, 8g): almond oil, jojoba oil, beeswax, shea butter, vanilla extract and vitamin E, in a vanilla or shea version.
  • Vilvah Natural Lemon Lip Balm (£6.99): organic shea butter, avocado oil, almond oil, unrefined beeswax and lemon essential oil.

For a rich, jar-style lip butter, Highborn London Superior Lip Butter (£22.50, 15ml, or a 50ml jar) is made with organic palm oil certified by the RSPO.

How to use a lip balm

  1. Start with clean, dry lips.
  2. Apply a thin layer with the stick or a clean fingertip, and reapply whenever lips feel dry.
  3. At night, use a thicker layer so it can sit on your lips while you sleep.
  4. Once or twice a week, use a lip scrub first. A balm spreads more evenly on smooth lips; our lip scrub guide explains how.
  5. In the sun, choose an SPF balm and reapply often.

Good to know

  • Try not to lick your lips: saliva dries quickly and leaves them drier than before.
  • Many balms contain beeswax. If you avoid it, check the Ingredients tab on each product before you buy.
  • Patch test balms with essential oils, such as the lemon and grapefruit balms, before first use.
  • Cracked or sore lips that do not settle after a week or two are worth showing to a pharmacist or your GP.
  • Lip balms make easy stocking fillers: see our stocking fillers guide.

nodes.title: Body wash or bath bar? Natural body care for dry skin
nodes.body:
Hot showers, central heating and cold wind all leave skin feeling tight in winter, and the wash you use is the first place to make a change. A natural body wash or a simple bath bar made from plant oils can clean skin without that squeaky, stripped feel, especially when it is followed by a good body lotion for dry skin. Here is how the two compare, what is inside the ones we stock, and a simple shower routine for dry skin.

Body wash or bath bar: what is the difference?

A bath bar is true soap: plant oils and butters turned into soap with lye, which is why sodium hydroxide appears on the ingredient list. None of it is left in the finished bar. Bars are compact, last a long time on a draining dish and come with little or no plastic.

A body wash is a liquid made with mild cleansers, usually derived from coconut or sugar, plus water-based ingredients such as plant waters (hydrosols) and glycerin. It is easy to share, works well on a loofah and is simple to use on dry or sensitive skin.

Neither is better for every skin. If your skin feels tight after showering, try a creamy wash or a butter-rich bar, keep showers short, and always follow with a lotion.

Natural body washes

  • Vilvah Goat Milk Body Wash (£15.99, 200ml) is made for dry and sensitive skin, with goat milk, virgin coconut oil, acai oil and glycerine in a chamomile water base, cleansed with coconut-derived coco glucoside. It has a low lather and a soft vanilla scent.
  • Deyga Wild Berry Body Wash (£16.99, 220ml) uses juniper berry and grapefruit hydrosols with a mild, fruity scent. Decyl glucoside from coconut gives a gentle lather, with glycerin and betaine from sugar beet. It is made without sulphates or parabens.
  • Deyga Activated Charcoal Body Wash (£13.99, 220ml) has coconut-shell charcoal in a cucumber and vetiver hydrosol base, also without sulphates. It gives a thorough, fresh-feeling wash after the gym; follow it with a lotion if your skin runs dry.

Browse every shower gel and body wash.

Bath bars made with plant oils

Deyga's bars share a base of extra virgin coconut oil, olive oil and castor oil, with a different hero ingredient in each:

  • Deyga Shea Saffron Bath Bar (£15.99, 100g): saffron, raw shea butter and sunflower oil, for a richer, creamy wash. A good pick for dry skin.
  • Deyga Rose Pink Clay Bath Bar (£14.99, 100g): rose hydrosol, pink kaolin clay and raw shea butter.
  • Deyga Spinach & Cucumber Bath Bar (£14.99, 100g): cucumber hydrosol and raw shea butter, coloured green with spirulina and matcha.
  • Deyga Charcoal Bath Bar (£10.99, 130g): activated charcoal, tea tree hydrosol and oil, aloe vera and unrefined shea butter. This is our charcoal soap.
  • Deyga Neem & Turmeric Bath Bar (£14.99, 100g): neem hydrosol and turmeric, two ingredients with a long history in Indian bathing traditions, with raw shea butter.

Prefer goat milk? Our goat milk soap guide covers the Vilvah bars.

A shower routine for dry skin

  1. Keep the water warm, not hot, and the shower short.
  2. Use a little wash or a light lather from the bar, and focus on the areas that need it.
  3. Exfoliate once or twice a week, not every day. Our body scrub guide explains how.
  4. Pat skin almost dry with a towel instead of rubbing.
  5. Apply a body lotion straight away, while skin is still slightly damp.

The body lotion for dry skin to follow

  • Vilvah Milk Body Lotion (£25.99, 250ml): oat milk, ceramide NP, olive squalane, jojoba oil and glycerin in a light, non-greasy texture. It contains fragrance.
  • Deyga Almond Milk Body Lotion (£14.99, 100ml): almond milk, cocoa butter, shea butter and almond oil, a handy size for travel.
  • The Vilvah Foot Cream & Body Lotion Kit (£37.99) pairs a body lotion with a foot cream for winter.

Need something richer for elbows, knees and shins? Read our body butter guide, and see the foot cream guide for dry heels. For a slower evening, anatomē Bath & Shower Oil with Roman Chamomile & Cornish Lavender (£68) can be smoothed over damp skin as the last step of a shower or added to a bath.

Good to know

  • Let bars dry between uses on a draining dish so they stay firm and last longer.
  • Patch test new products before first use, especially those with essential oils, such as the tea tree in the charcoal bar.
  • Charcoal washes and bars can feel more thorough; on dry skin, use them a few times a week rather than every day.
  • Skin that stays very dry, itchy, cracked or sore despite moisturising is worth showing to a pharmacist or your GP.

nodes.title: Deyga Beetroot Lip Balm: stick or pot, what is in it, and is it worth it?
nodes.body:
Quick answer: the Deyga Beetroot Lip Balm comes as a 10g pot (£10.99) and a 5.5g twist-up stick (£13.99), and both have exactly the same seven ingredients. The pot works out at about £1.10 per gram and the stick at about £2.54 per gram, so the pot is the better value and the stick is the tidier one to carry. It is a moisturising balm with a sheer beetroot tint. It has no SPF, and no lip balm can promise to lighten your lips.

What is in Deyga Beetroot Lip Balm?

The full ingredient list, in pack order, is the same for the Classic pot and the stick:

  1. Beetroot extract (listed as Beta vulgaris, with its Sanskrit name, paldka): the only colour in the list, which gives the sheer pink tint.
  2. Almond oil: a light oil that helps the balm glide.
  3. Avocado oil: a richer oil for a cushioned feel.
  4. Jojoba oil: a light liquid wax.
  5. Shea butter: a soft plant butter.
  6. Refined beeswax: sets the balm and holds it on the lips.
  7. Vitamin E.

That is it: no water, no added fragrance and no preservative in the list, because a balm made only of oils, butter and wax does not need one. Because of the beeswax it is not vegan, and the almond oil matters if you have a nut allergy.

Stick or pot: which should you buy?

  • Price: pot £10.99 for 10g (about £1.10/g); stick £13.99 for 5.5g (about £2.54/g). Gram for gram the stick costs roughly 2.3 times as much.
  • Packs of two: two pots are £20.99 (about £1.05/g) and two sticks £26.99 (about £2.45/g).
  • Applying: the pot needs a fingertip; the stick twists up and goes straight on, which is easier on the move, in gloves or without a mirror.
  • Colour: the same tint in both. With the stick, a second swipe builds it; with the pot, dab a little more.
  • Cold days: the stick slips into a coat pocket; the pot is handy on a bedside table for a thicker layer at night.

Choose the pot for value and for night-time use. Choose the stick if you will actually carry it and reapply through the day.

Does beetroot lip balm lighten dark lips?

You will see that claim online, including on some brand pages. We do not make it. Beetroot extract gives this balm a tint, so lips look pinker while it is on, and the oils and butter leave them feeling soft. That is a cosmetic effect that lasts while you wear it. Lips can darken for many reasons, from sun to smoking to medicines; if your lips change colour, or a patch is new or changing, show it to a pharmacist or your GP.

Is the Deyga Beetroot Lip Balm worth it?

It is worth it if you want:

  • a short, readable ingredient list with no added fragrance;
  • a sheer, natural-looking tint rather than a lipstick colour;
  • a balm that feels cushioned rather than waxy.

Look elsewhere if you need sun protection (it has no SPF), a strong colour, or a vegan balm. For daytime outdoors, pair it with Vilvah Milk Lip Balm SPF 30 PA+++ (£9.99). If you would rather skip the tint, Deyga Shea Butter Lip Balm (£9.99) is the plain everyday choice.

How to use it

  1. Start with clean, dry lips.
  2. Once or twice a week, use a lip scrub first: Deyga Mint Lip Scrub (£12.99) or Deyga Strawberry Lip Scrub (£10.99), both sugar in avocado and almond oils with shea butter.
  3. Apply the balm in a thin layer; add a second for more tint.
  4. Reapply whenever lips feel dry, and add a thicker layer at night.

Our lip scrub guide explains how often to scrub, and our lip balm guide compares SPF, tinted and natural balms from every brand we stock.

Deyga lip sets with the beetroot balm

  • Deyga Soft Lip Combo (£17.99): Mint Lip Scrub with the Classic pot, less than the £23.98 they cost separately.
  • Deyga Nourished Lip Care Kit (£25.99): Strawberry Lip Scrub with the Classic pot.
  • Deyga Nourished Lips Stick Kit (£27.99): Strawberry Lip Scrub with the stick.

Buying Deyga in the UK

Swansura is an official UK partner of Deyga, so every balm is genuine and ships from our UK stock, with no import charge to pay on delivery. UK delivery is free over £40, and the full ingredient list is on every product page. New to the brand? Read Deyga Organics in the UK, compare the two Indian brands we stock in Deyga or Vilvah, or shop all Deyga and every lip balm.

nodes.title: Deyga Organics in the UK: the brand, the ingredients and where to start
nodes.body:
Quick answer: Deyga, often searched as Deyga Organics, is an Indian natural care brand that makes skin, lip, body, foot and hair care with plant-based ingredients, many of which the brand says are grown on its own farm in India. It is best known for its beetroot lip balm, charcoal face wash and zinc oxide sunscreen. Swansura is an official UK partner of Deyga, so you can buy the range from UK stock, with free UK delivery over £40.

Is Deyga the same as Deyga Organics?

Yes. Deyga and Deyga Organics are the same brand and the same products; you will see both names on packs and online. On our site the range sits under Deyga.

What makes Deyga different?

The clearest way to understand any brand is its ingredient lists, and Deyga's are unusually readable:

  • Short lists. The Beetroot Lip Balm has seven ingredients and the Pure Rose Water Toner two: rose and distilled water.
  • Plant names in Sanskrit. Many lists add the traditional Indian name next to the Latin one, such as Satapatrika for rose, Kanya for aloe and Paldka for beetroot.
  • Plant waters. Several products are built on hydrosols (plant waters): tea tree in the Charcoal Face Wash, citrus in the Vitamin C Foaming Face Wash, rice water in the Rice Water Shampoo.
  • Mild coconut- and corn-derived cleansers such as decyl glucoside and sodium cocoyl glycinate in the washes and shampoos.

Two things worth knowing: some Deyga washes and shampoos list an added fragrance (marked IFRA approved), and several products use nut oils such as almond. The full ingredient list is on every Deyga product page on our site, so you can check before you buy.

Where to start with Deyga

Lips

The Beetroot Lip Balm Classic (from £10.99) is the product most people know Deyga for: a tinted balm with no added fragrance. Our guide Deyga Beetroot Lip Balm: stick or pot compares the two versions and the price per gram. The Soft Lip Combo (£17.99) adds a mint sugar scrub.

Face

  • Oat Milk Face Wash (£12.99): oat milk and kaolin with coconut-derived cleansers.
  • Charcoal Face Wash (from £12.99): coconut-shell charcoal in tea tree hydrosol.
  • Vitamin C Foaming Face Wash (£15.99): ascorbyl glucoside, a stable form of vitamin C, in citrus waters.
  • Pure Rose Water Toner (£11.99): rose and distilled water only.
  • 2% Hyaluronic Acid Serum (£22.99): sodium hyaluronate with aloe, centella and panthenol.
  • Deyga Sunscreen (from £16.99): a zinc oxide sunscreen in SPF 30 or SPF 50, with raspberry, carrot seed and sunflower oils.

Prefer a set? The Best Selling Face Care Kit (£28.99) puts a routine in one box. Our face wash guide and face serum guide help you choose by skin type.

Body and feet

Chocolate Body Butter (£13.99) is cocoa powder, shea butter, almond and jojoba oils and cocoa butter, with no water in the list. Deyga's handmade bath bars, such as Shea Saffron (£15.99), are true soaps made with coconut and olive oils, and the Mini Foot Spa Combo (£35.99) boxes a foot soak, scrub and butter. See our body butter guide, body wash and bath bar guide and foot cream guide.

Hair

Rice Water Shampoo (from £10.99) pairs with Soy Milk Conditioner (from £11.99), made with soybean extract, argan oil and panthenol. The Deyga Hair Care Kit (£36.99) adds Deyga's Hair Growth Oil, a coconut, almond and castor oil blend with amla, bhringraj and hibiscus. Our hair oil guide and natural shampoo guide explain how to use them.

Is Deyga a good brand?

That depends on what you want, and we sell it, so here are the facts rather than a verdict. Deyga publishes full ingredient lists, keeps most of them short and leans on plant oils, butters and hydrosols. It does not suit everyone: some products contain added fragrance or essential oils, several contain nut oils, the lip balms contain beeswax, and the bath bars are true soap. Patch test anything new, and if you have a skin condition, ask a pharmacist or GP first. We do not publish invented reviews; real customer reviews appear on each product page.

Buying Deyga in the UK

  • Genuine stock: Swansura is an official UK partner of Deyga.
  • Ships from the UK: no waiting for an overseas parcel and no import charge on delivery.
  • Delivery: free UK delivery over £40, and £5 off orders over £70 with code SAVE5.
  • Returns: unopened items within 14 days of delivery.

Looking for Deyga alternatives?

Vilvah is the other Indian natural brand we stock as an official UK partner, known for goat milk and botanical care. Read Vilvah in the UK, compare the two in Deyga or Vilvah, or see our Indian skincare in the UK guide. Shop all Deyga or the wider natural skincare range.

nodes.title: Vilvah Milk Drops serum: what is in it, 20ml or 40ml, and is it worth it?
nodes.body:
Quick answer: Vilvah Milk Drops is a light, water-based gel serum with eleven ingredients, led by aloe vera juice, betaine, glycerin and hyaluronic acid, plus alpha arbutin, a brown seaweed extract and rice milk extract. The milk in the name is rice milk extract: there is no dairy in the list. It comes in 20ml (£21.99, about £1.10 per ml) and 40ml (£30.99, about £0.77 per ml), so the 40ml is the better value if you use it daily.

What is in Vilvah Milk Drops?

The full ingredient list, in pack order:

  1. Aqua (water): the base of the gel.
  2. Aloe vera juice: a watery plant juice that gives a light, cool feel.
  3. Betaine: from sugar beet, it helps skin feel moisturised.
  4. Glycerin: a humectant that draws water into the skin's surface.
  5. Xanthan gum: thickens the serum into a gel.
  6. Hyaluronic acid: holds water, so skin feels plump and hydrated.
  7. Caprylic/capric triglyceride: a light, coconut-derived emollient.
  8. Cystoseira tamariscifolia extract: a brown seaweed extract.
  9. Alpha arbutin: a stable form of arbutin, a molecule found in plants such as bearberry.
  10. Rice milk extract: the milk in Milk Drops.
  11. Sodium benzoate and potassium sorbate: the preservatives.

Things the list does not contain: added fragrance, essential oils, alcohol, silicones or oils beyond the light triglyceride, and no animal-derived ingredients.

Is Milk Drops a brightening serum?

Vilvah names it a brightening serum, and you will see that word on packs and online. We describe what is in it rather than promise a result: day to day it works as a lightweight, hydrating layer that sits well under moisturiser and makeup. We cannot promise any change to dark spots or skin tone. If a patch of pigmentation is new, changing or worrying you, show it to a pharmacist or your GP, and whatever serum you use, daily sunscreen is the step that matters most.

20ml or 40ml: which size?

  • 20ml (£21.99): a good size to try it, or for travel.
  • 40ml (£30.99): about £0.77 per ml against £1.10 for the 20ml, and less than two 20ml bottles (£43.98).

At two to three drops morning and night, either size lasts a good while. Both are the same formula.

How to use Milk Drops

  1. Cleanse: Vilvah Fragrance-Free Cream Face Wash (£9.99) or the powder-to-foam Milk Powder Face Wash (£13.99).
  2. Tone if you like: Vilvah Milk Face Toner (£19.99) contains glycolic acid, so start it every other day.
  3. Press two or three drops of Milk Drops over the face and neck.
  4. Moisturise: Vilvah Ultra Moisturising Cream (£25.99) or your usual cream.
  5. In the morning, finish with sunscreen such as Vilvah Skin Finish Sunscreen SPF 50 PA+++ (£17.99).

Our face serum guide explains layering serums, and our toner guide and moisturiser guide help you choose the steps around it. Patch test before first use.

Milk Drops or Vilvah Better Ageing Serum?

  • Milk Drops: water-based gel; aloe, hyaluronic acid, alpha arbutin, rice milk extract. Light, for morning and evening.
  • Better Ageing Serum (£28.99, 20ml): a silkier serum with bakuchiol, niacinamide, ceramides, hyaluronic acid, pomegranate seed oil and olive squalane. Vilvah suggests it for evenings.

Many people use both: Milk Drops in the morning and Better Ageing at night. The Vilvah AM PM Serum Kit (£46.99) boxes the two together.

Kits with Milk Drops

  • Vilvah Milk Face Kit (£44.99): Milk Drops with the Milk Mud Mask, a kaolin clay mask with oat milk and saffron extracts.
  • Vilvah Skin Hydration Kit (£45.99): Milk Drops with the Milk Face Toner.
  • Vilvah AM PM Serum Kit (£46.99): Milk Drops with Better Ageing Serum.

Is Vilvah Milk Drops worth it?

It is worth it if you want a light, fragrance-free hydrating serum with a short list that layers easily under other products. Skip it if you want a rich, oily texture (choose Better Ageing) or a vitamin C serum (see our face serum guide). Real customer reviews appear on the product page; we do not publish invented ones.

Buying Vilvah in the UK

Swansura is an official UK partner of Vilvah, so every bottle is genuine and ships from UK stock with no import charge on delivery. UK delivery is free over £40. New to the brand? Read Vilvah in the UK, compare it with Deyga in Deyga or Vilvah, or shop all Vilvah and every face serum.

nodes.title: Versace perfume: Eros, Eros Pour Femme, Dylan Blue and Yellow Diamond compared
nodes.body:
Versace's fragrances split neatly in two: the Eros family, warm and sweet for him and bright and floral for her, and a set of fresher scents built on citrus, water and woods. Here is every Versace perfume we stock, with its notes, the sizes on offer and who each one suits.

Versace Eros: mint, apple and vanilla

Versace Eros Eau de Toilette (£68.99, 200ml) is a men's fragrance built on contrast. Mint, Italian lemon, mandarin and candied apple open it; geranium, clary sage and an amber note sit in the heart; and two cedarwoods, vetiver, patchouli, sandalwood and vanilla make the base. It starts cool and sweet, then settles warm and woody. A natural pick for nights out, parties and the colder months.

Versace Eros Parfum

Versace Eros Parfum (from £68.99, 100ml or 200ml) is the darker, more resinous version. Italian lemon, mandarin, litsea cubeba, elemi and black pepper open it; pomarose, Egyptian geranium, lavender and clary sage form the heart; and benzoin, cashmeran, patchouli, vanilla and vetiver sit underneath. Where the eau de toilette leans on mint and apple, the parfum leans on pepper, lavender and resin.

Eros eau de toilette or Eros Parfum? Choose the eau de toilette if you like the minty, sweet apple opening; choose the parfum for a spicier, deeper scent. A parfum holds a higher share of fragrance oils than an eau de toilette, so it feels richer and sits closer to the skin. Our guide to extrait vs eau de parfum explains the labels.

Versace Eros Pour Femme

Eros Pour Femme is a different perfume from the men's Eros, not a softer version of it. It comes in two strengths with different notes:

  • Eros Pour Femme Eau de Parfum (£59.99, 100ml): Sicilian lemon, Calabrian bergamot and pomegranate, then lemon flower, jasmine sambac and peony, over sandalwood, amber and musk. Bright at first, then floral and polished.
  • Eros Pour Femme Eau de Toilette Miniature (£13.99, 5ml): Sicilian lemon, mandarin, raspberry sorbet and white currant, then freesia, magnolia, jasmine petals and orange blossom, over ambrox, white patchouli and musk. Juicier and lighter, an easy daytime scent.

Versace Dylan Blue Pour Homme

Versace Dylan Blue Pour Homme Eau de Toilette Miniature (£13.99, 5ml) opens with water notes, fig leaves, bergamot and grapefruit. Violet leaves, patchouli, papyrus, black pepper and ambroxan sit in the heart, with musk, tonka bean, saffron and frankincense underneath. It starts fresh and aquatic and dries down darker and woodier, so it works for the day and for evenings.

Versace Man Eau Fraîche

Versace Man Eau Fraîche Eau de Toilette Miniature (£13.99, 5ml) is the crispest Versace for men: white lemon, rosewood and star fruit, then tarragon, cedar leaves and clary sage, over musk, amber and sycamore wood. Clean and airy, it suits hot days, holidays and the gym bag.

Versace Yellow Diamond

Versace Yellow Diamond Eau de Toilette (£52.99, 90ml) is a sunny floral for women. Citron, pear sorbet, neroli and bergamot open it; water lily, freesia, orange blossom and mimosa form a soft heart; and amber wood, palo santo and musk sit quietly underneath. Light, fruity and slightly powdery, it is a spring and summer scent, and an easy one for the office.

Which Versace perfume should you choose?

  • A sweet, warm scent for him: Versace Eros Eau de Toilette.
  • A deeper, spicier version: Versace Eros Parfum.
  • A fresh scent that turns woody: Dylan Blue Pour Homme.
  • Something light and citrusy for him: Man Eau Fraîche.
  • A bright floral for her: Eros Pour Femme Eau de Parfum, or the eau de toilette for a fruitier, lighter take.
  • A soft, sunny floral for her: Yellow Diamond.
  • Not sure yet: start with a 5ml miniature at £13.99.

If you like the fresh, marine side of Dylan Blue, Paco Rabanne Invictus Eau de Toilette (£78.99, 200ml) has sea notes and grapefruit over guaiac wood and patchouli. It is a different perfume, not a copy; our Paco Rabanne guide compares the whole range.

Good to know

  • The 5ml miniatures make easy stocking fillers: see our mini perfume sets guide for more.
  • Buying a gift? Our perfume gift sets guide has more Christmas ideas.
  • Every bottle is 100% authentic and dispatched from the UK, with free UK delivery over £40.

nodes.title: Narciso Rodriguez perfume: For Her, Musc Noir, All of Me and Bleu Noir compared
nodes.body:
Narciso Rodriguez fragrances are built around one note above all: musk. Each line wraps it in something different, from peach and rose to plum and suede or white flowers. Here is every Narciso Rodriguez perfume we stock, with its notes, the sizes on offer and who each one suits.

Narciso Rodriguez For Her

Narciso Rodriguez For Her is the one most people search for, and it comes in two versions with different notes:

  • For Her Eau de Parfum (from £25.99, 10ml or 50ml): rose and peach, then musk and amber, over patchouli and sandalwood. Soft, warm and rosy. Currently out of stock: use Notify me on the page and we will email you when it is back.
  • For Her Eau de Toilette (50ml or 100ml): African orange flower, osmanthus and bergamot, then musk and amber, over vetiver, vanilla and patchouli. Brighter and more floral at the start. Not available to buy at present.

The musk family: Pure Musc, Musc Noir and Musc Noir Rose

  • Pure Musc For Her Eau de Parfum (£25.99, 10ml): jasmine and orange blossom, then musk, over cashmeran. The cleanest and simplest of the line, a gentle, skin-like musk for every day.
  • Musc Noir For Her Eau de Parfum (from £25.99, 10ml or 50ml): plum, then musk and heliotrope, over suede. Darker and more velvety, a good autumn and winter choice.
  • Musc Noir Rose For Her Eau de Parfum (£25.99, 10ml): bergamot and pink peppercorn, then musk and tuberose, over vanilla, patchouli and suede leather. A floral, slightly spicy take on Musc Noir.

Narciso Cristal and Narciso Ambree

Both are 10ml eau de parfums at £25.99:

  • Narciso Cristal: freesia, orange blossom and bergamot, then rose, jasmine and musk, over cashmeran, cedar, benzoin and amber. Bright and floral.
  • Narciso Ambree: frangipani, ylang-ylang and white flowers, then musk and amber, over cashmeran, cedar and vanilla. Warmer and creamier.

Narciso Rodriguez All of Me

All of Me Eau de Parfum (£69.99, 90ml) opens on magnolia, with rose and Bourbon geranium in the heart and musk and sandalwood in the base. Geranium gives the rose a fresh, slightly green lift, so it reads clean and polished rather than sweet. An easy everyday signature for any season.

For Him Bleu Noir

For Him Bleu Noir Eau de Toilette (£46.99, 50ml) is the Narciso for men: cardamom and nutmeg, then musk, over vetiver, cedarwood, ebony wood and amber. Spiced and woody, it works at the office and through the cooler months.

Which Narciso Rodriguez perfume should you choose?

  • A soft, rosy musk: For Her Eau de Parfum.
  • The cleanest musk: Pure Musc For Her.
  • A darker, velvety musk for winter: Musc Noir, or Musc Noir Rose for a floral version.
  • A fresh, polished floral: All of Me.
  • A creamy white-flower scent: Narciso Ambree.
  • For him: For Him Bleu Noir.
  • Not sure yet: the 10ml sizes at £25.99 let you try one before a bigger bottle, and make easy stocking fillers.

If musk is what you love, Attar Collection Floral Musk Eau de Parfum (£46.99, 100ml, unisex) pairs tagetes and jasmine with amber, caramel and white musk over sandalwood and myrrh. It is a different perfume, warmer and sweeter than the Narciso musks.

Good to know

  • Eau de parfum or eau de toilette? Our guide to extrait vs eau de parfum explains the labels.
  • Buying a gift? See our mini perfume sets guide and perfume gift sets guide.
  • Every bottle is 100% authentic and dispatched from the UK, with free UK delivery over £40.
