nodes.title: Issey Miyake L'Eau d'Issey: the original and its newer versions compared
nodes.body:
L'Eau d'Issey is Issey Miyake's watery floral for women, and over the years it has grown into a whole family: a magnolia version, a rose version, a sweeter nectar version, and the rain-scented A Drop d'Issey. Here is what the original smells like, how each newer version differs, and which Issey Miyake fragrance to choose.

What does the original L'Eau d'Issey smell like?

The original L'Eau d'Issey Eau de Toilette is built around water and flowers. Its listed notes open with lotus, rose, freesia, cyclamen, melon and calone (a fresh, watery note), move to lily of the valley, lily, water peony and carnation, and settle on musk, tuberose, woods, osmanthus, cedar, sandalwood and amber. The result is clean and airy rather than sweet. We list the 50ml eau de toilette, which is not available to buy at present; the newer versions below are in stock.

The newer L'Eau d'Issey versions

Eau & Magnolia

L'Eau d'Issey Eau & Magnolia Eau de Toilette Intense (from £43.99, 50ml or 100ml) is the simplest: bergamot, then magnolia and rose, over sandalwood and musk. A soft, creamy floral that stays close to the original's clean feel.

Rose & Rose

L'Eau d'Issey Rose & Rose Eau de Parfum Intense (£48.99, 90ml) is the richest of the family. Raspberry, pear and pink pepper open it; Bulgarian rose, rose and osmanthus fill the heart; and cashmere wood, amber and patchouli make the base. Fruity at first, then a deep, warm rose.

Pure Pétale de Nectar

L'Eau d'Issey Pure Pétale de Nectar Eau de Toilette (£43.99, 90ml) is the sweetest: pear and honey, then rose and peony, over cashmeran, white musk and sandalwood. A soft, honeyed floral for anyone who finds the original too watery.

A Drop d'Issey

A Drop d'Issey Eau de Parfum Fraiche (£44.99, 90ml) opens on a rain accord, like the air after a shower, with lilac and Damask rose in the heart and sandalwood and musk underneath. It keeps the brand's focus on water but with a lighter, cooler feel, and suits spring, summer and the office.

For him: Le Sel d'Issey

Le Sel d'Issey Eau de Toilette (£18.99, 10ml) is a fresh men's scent built on sea salt and ginger, with vetiver and sand vetiver in the heart and cedarwood and oakmoss in the base: dry, mineral and slightly spicy. The 10ml size is an easy way to try it. We also list L'Eau d'Issey Pour Homme and Pour Homme Wood & Wood, which are not available at present.

Which Issey Miyake fragrance should you choose?

  • Clean and close to the original: Eau & Magnolia.
  • A deeper, warmer rose: Rose & Rose.
  • Something sweeter and honeyed: Pure Pétale de Nectar.
  • Light, cool and fresh: A Drop d'Issey.
  • For him: Le Sel d'Issey.

Other fresh florals to try

If you like L'Eau d'Issey's watery, airy style, these are different perfumes in a similar mood:

  • Versace Yellow Diamond Eau de Toilette (£52.99, 90ml): citron, pear sorbet, neroli and bergamot, then water lily, freesia and mimosa.
  • Davidoff Cool Water Reborn Intense Eau de Parfum (£18.99, 50ml): bergamot and green notes, a rose heart, then vetiver, woods and musk.
  • Versace Eros Pour Femme Eau de Toilette Miniature (£13.99, 5ml): lemon, mandarin, raspberry sorbet and white currant, then freesia, magnolia and jasmine.

Good to know

  • Eau de toilette or eau de parfum? Our guide to extrait vs eau de parfum explains the labels.
  • Buying a gift? See our perfume gift sets guide.
  • Every bottle is 100% authentic and dispatched from the UK, with free UK delivery over £40.

nodes.title: Winter skincare for dry skin: a simple Vilvah and Deyga routine
nodes.body:
Cold air outside and central heating inside both dry the air, and skin often feels it first: a tight face after washing, rough patches on legs and elbows, dry lips. The fix is usually not more products but slightly different ones. Here is a simple winter skincare routine for dry skin, using Vilvah and Deyga, with what is in each product.

1. Cleanse gently

In winter, a cream or low-foam cleanser leaves skin feeling more comfortable than a strong foaming wash. Vilvah Fragrance-Free Cream Face Wash (£9.99, 100ml) uses mild cleansers (disodium cocoyl glutamate, coco-glucoside) with glycerine, banana fruit extract and hydrolysed wheat protein, and has no added fragrance. Deyga Oat Milk Face Wash (£12.99, 100ml) is built on oat milk with betaine, provitamin B5 and kaolin; it does contain fragrance. Wash with lukewarm rather than hot water, and pat dry. Our guide to face wash for your skin type has more options.

2. Add a hydrating serum

A watery serum on slightly damp skin, before your cream, adds a light layer of moisture. Deyga 2% Hyaluronic Acid Serum (£22.99, 20ml) pairs sodium hyaluronate with glycerine, panthenol, aloe vera and centella asiatica, without fragrance. Our face serum guide explains how to layer one.

3. Switch to a richer moisturiser

If your summer moisturiser feels too light, winter is the time for a richer cream.

  • Deyga Deep Moisturising Face Cream (£18.99, 30g): centella asiatica, cardamom, marula oil, almond oil and shea butter, with glycerine. A short, butter-rich list.
  • Vilvah Ultra Moisturising Cream (£25.99, 50ml): glycerine and olive squalane, with bamboo, goji berry and sophora extracts and a hint of white lily essential oil.

Apply morning and night. Our guide to moisturiser for your skin type compares more creams.

4. Keep wearing SPF

Winter sun is lower, but UV still reaches the skin, especially on bright days, in snow and at altitude. Vilvah Skin Finish Sunscreen SPF 50 PA+++ (£17.99) is a light sunscreen whose list also includes glycerine, sodium hyaluronate and ceramides. Apply it as the last step in the morning.

5. Body: lotion by day, butter by night

  • Vilvah Milk Body Lotion (£25.99, 250ml): oat milk, ceramide NP, olive squalane, coconut oil and jojoba oil. Light enough to wear under clothes every morning.
  • Deyga Chocolate Body Butter (£13.99, 100g): cocoa powder, shea butter, almond oil, jojoba oil, cocoa butter and vitamin E, with no water in the list. Richer, for elbows, knees and shins at night.

Apply either straight after a shower, while skin is still slightly damp. Our body butter guide and body wash guide cover the rest of the shower routine.

6. Lips

Lips have no oil glands of their own, so they dry out first. Deyga Beetroot Lip Balm (from £10.99, 10g) is made with beetroot extract, almond, avocado and jojoba oils, shea butter and beeswax, with a sheer tint. On bright or snowy days, Vilvah Milk Lip Balm SPF 30 PA+++ (£9.99) uses zinc oxide and titanium dioxide. Our lip balm guide compares them all.

7. Feet

Boots and heating are hard on heels. Vilvah Foot Care Cream (£16, 100ml) is rich in shea, avocado, mango and cocoa butters with sunflower, argan and kalonji oils and peppermint oil. Deyga Foot Butter (£12.99, 40g) is a waterless balm of coconut oil, olive oil, beeswax and vitamin E; apply it at night under cotton socks. See our foot cream guide for an at-home pedicure.

Hair

Dry indoor air can leave lengths feeling rough too. Once a week, Vilvah Goat Milk Hair Mask (£31.99) pairs goat milk with ceramides and argan oil. Our frizzy hair guide has more.

Small habits that help

  • Shorter, warm showers rather than long hot ones.
  • Moisturise within a few minutes of washing, while skin is damp.
  • Patch test any new product, one at a time.
  • See a pharmacist or your GP if dryness comes with redness, itching or cracks that do not settle.

nodes.title: Peptide serum and bakuchiol serum: what they are and how to use them
nodes.body:
Peptides and bakuchiol are two of the most searched serum ingredients in the UK, often alongside ceramides. They do different jobs and suit different routines. Here is what each one is, how to use a peptide serum or a bakuchiol serum, and the serums we stock that contain them.

What are peptides?

Peptides are short chains of amino acids, the building blocks of proteins. In skincare they are made in the lab or taken from plants, and they usually appear in serums and creams in small amounts. Different peptides have different trade names, such as Matrixyl or Argireline, so a peptide serum often lists several of them together.

Peptide serums we stock

  • Highborn London YOUTHBOOST Peptide Serum (£94) combines four peptide ingredients in one lightweight, vegan-friendly serum: Matrixyl 3000, Argireline, Tripeptide-5 and Copper Tripeptide-1 (a copper peptide).
  • Caviar Serum with 24K Gold (£34.99) is a Swansura Selection serum with tremella polysaccharide, beta-glucan and sodium hyaluronate for hydration, aloe vera and oat kernel extract, amino acids and peptides, carnosine and 24K gold leaf.

What is bakuchiol?

Bakuchiol is a plant-derived ingredient, taken from the seeds of the babchi plant (Psoralea corylifolia). It is often chosen instead of retinol by people who prefer a plant-based ingredient. It can usually be used morning and night; as with any new serum, patch test first.

Bakuchiol serums we stock

  • Highborn London Bakuchiol Youth Elixir (£99) is a bakuchiol serum made in England for mature and sensitive skin, for morning or evening use.
  • Vilvah Better Ageing Serum (£28.99, 20ml) has the longest list: bakuchiol and a natural peptide extract (from sacha inchi seed), with blue pea flower extract, pomegranate seed oil, hyaluronic acid, two ceramides, niacinamide and olive squalane. It brings peptides, bakuchiol and ceramides together in one bottle, in a light texture.

What are ceramides?

Ceramides are lipids that occur naturally in the outer layer of skin. In skincare they are added to help skin feel smooth and comfortable, and they pair well with peptides or bakuchiol. Highborn London MOISTUREBURST Hydrating Glow Ceramide Serum (from £57, 30ml or 50ml) is a lightweight ceramide serum for dry, dehydrated and mature skin, made to layer under moisturiser.

How to use a peptide or bakuchiol serum

  1. Cleanse and, if you use one, apply toner. Our face wash guide and toner guide help you choose.
  2. Apply 2 or 3 drops of serum to the face and neck and press it in.
  3. Follow with moisturiser, such as Highborn London Imperial Moisturiser (£46). See moisturiser for your skin type.
  4. In the morning, finish with SPF, for example Vilvah Skin Finish Sunscreen SPF 50 PA+++ (£17.99).

Use one new serum at a time, so you know what suits your skin. One serum in the morning and one at night is plenty for most people.

Can you use peptides and bakuchiol together?

Yes, they are commonly layered, and the Vilvah Better Ageing Serum already contains both. If you use two serums, apply the thinner, watery one first and the richer one after, or use one in the morning and one at night.

Ready-made routines

  • The Vilvah Better Ageing Kit (£48.99) pairs the Better Ageing Serum with the Ultra Moisturising Cream (glycerine, olive squalane, bamboo and goji berry extracts) for an evening routine.
  • The Vilvah Night Repair Kit (£42.99) pairs the same serum with an Under Eye Cream made with shea butter, sunflower seed oil, bamboo and goji berry extracts.

Good to know

  • Patch test any new serum on your jaw or inner arm for 24 hours.
  • Pregnant or breastfeeding? Check new skincare ingredients with your GP or pharmacist first.
  • Stinging, redness or itching that lasts is worth showing to a pharmacist or your GP.
  • For vitamin C, hyaluronic acid and niacinamide, see our face serum guide.
